akhfash:1-1.t: He said ﴿وَٱلنَّازِعَاتِ غَرْقاً﴾: He swore — and Allah knows best — upon ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِّمَن يَخْشَىٰ﴾. And if you wish, you make it upon ﴿يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ ٱلرَّاجِفَةُ﴾ [6] ﴿قُلُوبٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَاجِفَةٌ﴾ [8] ﴿وَٱلنَّازِعَاتِ﴾. And if you wish, you make ﴿وَٱلنَّازِعَاتِ﴾ (sworn) for ﴿يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ ٱلرَّاجِفَةُ﴾ ﴿تَتْبَعُهَا ٱلرَّادِفَةُ﴾ [7], the lām having been dropped. And it is as He, exalted be His mention, said, and as He willed it to be, in this and in all matters.

akhfash:10-11.t: And He said ﴿أَإِنَّا لَمَرْدُودُونَ فِي ٱلْحَافِرَةِ﴾ ﴿أَإِذَا كُنَّا عِظَاماً﴾: as if He meant "shall we be returned when we are bones?" (أَنُرَدُّ إِذَا كُنَّا عِظاماً). As for whoever said ﴿أاِنَّا﴾ and ﴿أَاإِذا كنا﴾ with the two hamzas together, separating them with an alif, he has only left implied the statement for which this was made an adverb (ẓarf), because it had been said to them "you will be raised and brought back" (إِنَّكُم تُبْعَثون وتُعادُون), so they said ﴿أإِذا كنا ترابا﴾ — at that time we will be brought back? This is part of the speech of the Arabs. Some of them say ﴿أَيِنَّا﴾ and ﴿أَيِذَا﴾, lightening the second (hamza), because two hamzas do not come together. The Kufans say "أإِنا" and "أَإِذا", combining the two hamzas. Ibn Abī Isḥāq used to combine the two hamzas in recitation, according to what has reached us. And some Arabs say "اللهمَّ اغفر لي خطائِئى" ("O Allah, forgive me my sins"), pronouncing both with hamza; this is rare, and it is in the dialect of Qays.

akhfash:16-16.t:
And He said ﴿بِٱلْوَادِ ٱلْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى﴾: whoever does not make it fully declinable (treating it as a diptote) makes it (the name of) a town or a tract of land; whoever makes it declinable makes it the name of a valley or a place. And some said: "No, rather it is declinable, and by ﴿طوى﴾ He means only a ṭuwan (a part) of the night", because you say "جِئْتُكَ بعدَ طُوًى من الليل" ("I came to you after a part of the night had passed"). And it is also said ﴿طِوىً﴾ with tanwīn, like "الثِّنى". The poet said [in the basīṭ metre; this is the two hundred and seventy-seventh verse cited as evidence]:
تَرى ثِنانَا إِذَا ما جاءَ بَدْأَهُمُ * وَبَدَأَهُم إِن أَتَانَا كانَ ثِنْياَنَا
(You see our second-rank man, when he comes, as their foremost; and their foremost, if he comes to us, is our second-rank.)
And الثِّنى*: it is the thing that is doubled (repeated).

akhfash:25-25.t: And He said ﴿فَأَخَذَهُ ٱللَّهُ نَكَالَ ٱلآخِرَةِ وَٱلأُوْلَىٰ﴾ because when He said ﴿أَخَذَه﴾ it is as if (He said) "He made an exemplary punishment of him" (نَكَّلَ لِهِ), so He brought the maṣdar (verbal noun) out accordingly. And you say "والله لأصْرِمَنَّكَ تركا بَيِّناً" ("by Allah, I will surely cut you off — a clear abandonment"). «[Translator's note: «نَكَّلَ لِهِ» is so written in the source; presumably «نَكَّلَ بِهِ».]»

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿وَالنَّازِعَاتِ﴾ the angels who wrench out the souls of the unbelievers ﴿غَرْقًا﴾ a violent wrenching,

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَالنَّاشِطَاتِ نَشْطًا﴾ the angels who draw out the souls of the believers, i.e. take them out gently,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَالسَّابِحَاتِ سَبْحًا﴾ the angels who glide from the heaven by His command, exalted is He, i.e. descend,

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿فَالسَّابِقَاتِ سَبْقًا﴾ the angels who race with the souls of the believers to Paradise,

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿فَالْمُدَبِّرَاتِ أَمْرًا﴾ the angels who manage the affairs of this world, i.e. descend with its management. The answer to these oaths is omitted, i.e. "you will surely be resurrected, O unbelievers of Mecca", and it is what governs

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الرَّاجِفَةُ﴾ the first blowing, by which everything quakes, i.e. is shaken; so it is described by what happens through it,

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿تَتْبَعُهَا الرَّادِفَةُ﴾ the second blowing; between the two are forty years; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الرَّاجِفَةُ; so the day is wide enough for the two blowings and other things, and thus it is valid as the adverb (ẓarf) for the resurrection, which occurs after the second.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿أَبْصَارُهَا خَاشِعَةٌ﴾ abased at the terror of what they see.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ i.e. the owners of the hearts and eyes, in mockery and denial of the resurrection: ﴿أَإِنَّا﴾ with both hamzas pronounced fully (taḥqīq), and with the second softened (tashīl), and with an alif inserted between them in both ways, in both places ﴿لَمَرْدُودُونَ فِي الْحَافِرَةِ﴾ i.e. shall we be returned to life after death? al-ḥāfira is a name for the beginning of a matter, and from it is "So-and-so returned on his ḥāfira", when he went back the way he came.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿أَإِذَا كُنَّا عِظَامًا نَخِرَةً﴾ — in one reading [نَاخِرَةً] — decayed and crumbled, shall we live?

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿قَالُوا تِلْكَ﴾ i.e. our return to life ﴿إِذًا﴾ if it be true, ﴿كَرَّةٌ﴾ a return ﴿خَاسِرَةٌ﴾ of loss.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿فَإِنَّمَا هِيَ﴾ i.e. the following [blast], after which comes the resurrection, ﴿زَجْرَةٌ﴾ a blowing ﴿وَاحِدَةٌ﴾ and when it is blown,

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿فَإِذَا هُمْ﴾ i.e. all creatures ﴿بِالسَّاهِرَةِ﴾ on the face of the earth, alive, after having been in its belly, dead.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿إِذْ نَادَاهُ رَبُّهُ بِالْوَادِ الْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى﴾ the name of the valley, with tanwīn and without it; and He said:

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿اذْهَبْ إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَى﴾ overstepped the limit in unbelief;

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿فَقُلْ هَلْ لَكَ﴾ I call you ﴿إِلَى أَنْ تَزَكَّى﴾ — in one reading with doubling of the zāy, by assimilation of the second tāʾ of the underlying form — to purify yourself of idolatry by testifying that there is no god but Allah,

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَأَهْدِيَكَ إِلَى رَبِّكَ﴾ guide you to knowledge of Him by proof ﴿فَتَخْشَى﴾ so that you fear Him.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿فَأَرَاهُ الْآيَةَ الْكُبْرَى﴾ of the nine signs, and it is the hand or the staff;

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ﴾ from faith ﴿يَسْعَى﴾ in the land with corruption;

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿فَحَشَرَ﴾ gathered the sorcerers and his troops ﴿فَنَادَى﴾

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿فَقَالَ أَنَا رَبُّكُمُ الْأَعْلَى﴾ there is no lord above me.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿فَأَخَذَهُ اللَّهُ﴾ destroyed him by drowning, ﴿نَكَالَ﴾ as the punishment ﴿الْآخِرَةِ﴾ i.e. of this [last] word ﴿وَالْأُولَى﴾ i.e. his saying before it: {مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرِي}; and between the two were forty years.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ﴾ which has been mentioned ﴿لَعِبْرَةً لِمَنْ يَخْشَى﴾ Allah the Exalted.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿أَأَنْتُمْ﴾ with both hamzas pronounced fully (taḥqīq), with the second changed to an alif, and with it softened (tashīl), with an alif inserted between the softened one and the other and without it; i.e. those who deny the resurrection; ﴿أَشَدُّ خَلْقًا أَمِ السَّمَاءُ﴾ more difficult in creation? ﴿بَنَاهَا﴾ an explanation of how it was created.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا﴾ an explanation of how it was built, i.e. He made its extent in the upward direction lofty; it is also said: سَمْكَهَا is its roof; ﴿فَسَوَّاهَا﴾ made it even, without flaw,

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿وَأَغْطَشَ لَيْلَهَا﴾ darkened it ﴿وَأَخْرَجَ ضُحَاهَا﴾ brought out the light of its sun; the night is annexed to it because it is its shadow, and the sun because it is its lamp.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ دَحَاهَا﴾ spread it out; it had been created before the heaven, without being spread out.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿أَخْرَجَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) with قَدْ implied, i.e. bringing out ﴿مِنْهَا مَاءَهَا﴾ by making its springs gush ﴿وَمَرْعَاهَا﴾ what livestock graze on, of trees and grass, and what people eat, of staple foods and fruits; applying "pasture" (al-marʿā) to it is a metaphor (istiʿāra).

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَالْجِبَالَ أَرْسَاهَا﴾ fixed them firmly on the face of the earth so that it would be still,

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿مَتَاعًا﴾ a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose) for an implied [verb], i.e. He did that as a provision; or a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. providing; ﴿لَكُمْ وَلِأَنْعَامِكُمْ﴾ plural of نَعَم, which are camels, cattle and sheep.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿فَإِذَا جَاءَتِ الطَّامَّةُ الْكُبْرَى﴾ the second blowing,

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنْسَانُ﴾ a badal (substitute) for إِذَا ﴿مَا سَعَى﴾ in this world, of good and evil,

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿وَبُرِّزَتِ﴾ is made manifest ﴿الْجَحِيمُ﴾ the burning Fire ﴿لِمَنْ يَرَى﴾ for everyone who sees; and the answer (jawāb) of إِذَا [is]:

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ﴾ his standing before Him ﴿وَنَهَى النَّفْسَ﴾ the one that commands [evil] ﴿عَنِ الْهَوَى﴾ which ruins, through following desires,

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿فَإِنَّ الْجَنَّةَ هِيَ الْمَأْوَى﴾ The gist of the answer is: the disobedient is in the Fire and the obedient is in Paradise.

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ﴾ i.e. the unbelievers of Mecca ﴿عَنِ السَّاعَةِ أَيَّانَ مُرْسَاهَا﴾ when will it occur and be established?

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿فِيمَ﴾ in what ﴿أَنْتَ مِنْ ذِكْرَاهَا﴾ i.e. you do not have knowledge of it, that you should mention it.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿إِلَى رَبِّكَ مُنْتَهَاهَا﴾ the ultimate knowledge of it; none but He knows it.

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مُنْذِرُ﴾ your warning benefits only ﴿مَنْ يَخْشَاهَا﴾ fears it.

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَهَا لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا﴾ in their graves ﴿إِلَّا عَشِيَّةً أَوْ ضُحَاهَا﴾ i.e. the evening of a day or its morning; annexing al-ḍuḥā to al-ʿashiyya is valid because of the connection between them, since they are the two ends of the day; and what makes the annexation fine is the word falling at a verse ending (fāṣila).

daas-irab:1-5.t: ﴿وَ﴾: the wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive; ﴿النَّازِعاتِ﴾: the thing sworn by, genitive (majrūr); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb of swearing; ﴿غَرْقاً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَالنَّاشِطاتِ نَشْطاً﴾, ﴿وَالسَّابِحاتِ سَبْحاً﴾, ﴿فَالسَّابِقاتِ سَبْقاً﴾: conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَالْمُدَبِّراتِ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿أَمْراً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

daas-irab:6-9.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿تَرْجُفُ الرَّاجِفَةُ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿تَتْبَعُهَا﴾: an imperfect verb and its object; ﴿الرَّادِفَةُ﴾: its agent; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿قُلُوبٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb annexed to one like it; ﴿واجِفَةٌ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of قلوب; ﴿أَبْصارُها خاشِعَةٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate); the clause is the khabar of قلوب, and the clause قلوب… is resumptive.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هم يقولون". ﴿أَإِنَّا﴾: the hamza is an interrogative particle, and inna and its noun; ﴿لَمَرْدُودُونَ﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) and its khabar; ﴿فِي الْحافِرَةِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them; the nominal clause is the maqūl (speech content) of the saying.

daas-irab:11-14.t: ﴿أَإِذا﴾: the hamza is an interrogative particle, and ﴿إِذا﴾ is a conditional adverb that does not put the verb in the jussive; ﴿كُنَّا عِظاماً﴾: kāna, its noun and its khabar (predicate); ﴿نَخِرَةً﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿قالُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿تِلْكَ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿إِذاً﴾: a particle of answer and requital with no governing effect; ﴿كَرَّةٌ﴾: khabar; ﴿خاسِرَةٌ﴾: adjective; the nominal clause is the maqūl (speech content) of the saying. ﴿فَإِنَّما﴾: the restraining particle (kāffa) and the restrained one (makfūfa), and the fāʾ is resumptive; ﴿هِيَ زَجْرَةٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ and its khabar; ﴿واحِدَةٌ﴾: adjective; the nominal clause is the maqūl of an omitted verb of saying, and the discourse is resumptive. ﴿فَإِذا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction and ﴿إذا﴾ is the particle of surprise (fujāʾiyya); ﴿هُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ; ﴿بِالسَّاهِرَةِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar.

daas-irab:15-17.t: ﴿هَلْ﴾: an interrogative particle; ﴿أَتاكَ﴾: a past verb and its object; ﴿حَدِيثُ﴾: fāʿil (agent); ﴿مُوسى﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِذْ﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿ناداهُ رَبُّهُ﴾: a past verb, its object and its agent; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿بِالْوادِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿الْمُقَدَّسِ﴾: naʿt (adjective); ﴿طُوىً﴾: badal (substitute) for الوادي. ﴿اذْهَبْ﴾: an imperative verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); the clause is explicative of the calling; ﴿إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ﴾: attached to the verb. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿طَغى﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:18-19.t: ﴿فَقُلْ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿هَلْ﴾: an interrogative particle; ﴿لَكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), the implied form being: "هل لك سبيل" (have you a way). ﴿إِلى﴾: a preposition; ﴿أَنْ﴾: a maṣdar-forming particle that puts the verb in the accusative; ﴿تَزَكَّى﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, its agent latent; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive by the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted mubtadaʾ; the implied nominal clause is the maqūl (speech content) of the saying.

daas-irab:20-23.t: ﴿فَأَراهُ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its first object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿الْآيَةَ﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿الْكُبْرى﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَكَذَّبَ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb whose agent is latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَعَصى﴾: conjoined to كذب. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿أَدْبَرَ﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿يَسْعى﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَحَشَرَ فَنادى﴾: both conjoined to what precedes them.

daas-irab:24-26.t: ﴿فَقالَ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَنَا رَبُّكُمُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); ﴿الْأَعْلى﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is the maqūl (speech content) of the saying. ﴿فَأَخَذَهُ اللَّهُ﴾: a past verb and its object, and the Name of Majesty is its agent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿نَكالَ الْآخِرَةِ﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), muḍāf to الآخرة; ﴿الْأُولى﴾: conjoined to الآخرة. ﴿إِنَّ﴾: a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters); ﴿فِي ذلِكَ﴾: the fronted khabar of inna; ﴿لَعِبْرَةً﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) and the postponed noun of inna; the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿لِمَنْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of عبرة; ﴿يَخْشى﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of من.

daas-irab:27-29.t: ﴿أَأَنْتُمْ﴾: the hamza is an interrogative particle; ﴿أَنْتُمْ أَشَدُّ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive; ﴿خَلْقاً﴾: tamyīz (specification). ﴿أَمِ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿السَّماءُ﴾: mubtadaʾ, its khabar omitted; the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بَناها﴾: a past verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿رَفَعَ﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent; ﴿سَمْكَها﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is explicative. ﴿فَسَوَّاها﴾: a past verb and its object, the agent being latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَأَغْطَشَ لَيْلَها﴾: a past verb and its object, the agent being latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَأَخْرَجَ ضُحاها﴾: conjoined to أغطش ليلها.

daas-irab:30-33.t:
﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb explained by what follows it; ﴿بَعْدَ ذلِكَ﴾: an adverb of time, muḍāf to ذلك. ﴿دَحاها﴾: a past verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause is explicative. ﴿أَخْرَجَ﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent; ﴿مِنْها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿ماءَها﴾: direct object; ﴿وَمَرْعاها﴾: conjoined to ماءها; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَالْجِبالَ أَرْساها﴾: parsed like the preceding one.
﴿مَتاعاً﴾: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); ﴿لَكُمْ﴾: attached to what precedes them; ﴿وَلِأَنْعامِكُمْ﴾: conjoined to لكم.

daas-irab:34-36.t: ﴿فَإِذا﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and إذا is a conditional adverb that does not put the verb in the jussive; ﴿جاءَتِ الطَّامَّةُ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted; ﴿الْكُبْرى﴾: naʿt (adjective) of الطامة; the verbal clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time, badal (substitute) for إذا; ﴿يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنْسانُ﴾: a past verb [Translator's note: so in the source; يتذكر is an imperfect verb] and its agent; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation; ﴿ما﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿سَعى﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَبُرِّزَتِ﴾: a passive past verb; ﴿الْجَحِيمُ﴾: its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لِمَنْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them; ﴿يَرى﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent; the clause is the ṣila of من.

daas-irab:37-39.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle and ﴿أما﴾ is a particle of condition and detailing; ﴿مَنْ﴾: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿طَغى﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of من; ﴿وَآثَرَ﴾: conjoined to طغى; ﴿الْحَياةَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾: naʿt (adjective). ﴿فَإِنَّ الْجَحِيمَ﴾: the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa), and inna and its noun; ﴿هِيَ﴾: a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿الْمَأْوى﴾: the khabar (predicate) of inna; the nominal clause is the khabar of من.

daas-irab:40-41.t: The two verses are conjoined to what precedes them, and their i'rab is clear.

daas-irab:42-45.t: ﴿يَسْئَلُونَكَ﴾: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; ﴿عَنِ السَّاعَةِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَيَّانَ﴾: an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative as an adverb of time, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿مُرْساها﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the second object of يسألونك. ﴿فِيمَ﴾: fronted khabar; ﴿أَنْتَ﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ; ﴿مِنْ ذِكْراها﴾: attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿إِلى رَبِّكَ﴾: fronted khabar; ﴿مُنْتَهاها﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّما﴾: the restraining particle (kāffa) and the restrained one (makfūfa); ﴿أَنْتَ مُنْذِرُ﴾: mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is resumptive; ﴿مَنْ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿يَخْشاها﴾: an imperfect verb and its object, the agent being latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of من.

daas-irab:46-46.t: ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ﴾: كأن and its noun; ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿يَرَوْنَها﴾: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا﴾: an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, the wāw being its agent; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of كأن, and the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿عَشِيَّةً﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿أَوْ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿ضُحاها﴾: conjoined to عشية.

dervis-irab:1-14.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الرَّاجِفَةُ) In al-Mukhtār: «al-rajfa is the earthquake; the earth rajafat, of the pattern of naṣara.» More of its meaning will come in the section on rhetoric.
(الرَّادِفَةُ) The one that follows. In al-Qāmūs: «radifahu, like samiʿahu and naṣarahu: he followed him, like ardafahu.»
(الْحافِرَةِ) The first state; they mean life after death. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: what is the true sense of this word? I say: one says "so-and-so returned in his ḥāfira", i.e. on his path by which he came, which he dug (ḥafarahā), i.e. left marks on by his walking in it; the marks of his feet were made a digging, just as it is said "his teeth were dug (ḥafarat), ḥafran" when decay has left its mark at their roots, and the line dug into rock. And it was called ḥāfira as it was said ʿīsha rāḍiya (a pleasing life), i.e. ascribed to digging and to pleasure, or as in their saying "your day is fasting". Then it was said of one who was in a matter, left it, and then returned to it: "he returned to his ḥāfira", i.e. to his way and his first state. He said:
أحافرة على صلع وشيب ... معاذ الله من سفه وعار»
(Back to the old ways, despite baldness and grey hair? Allah forbid such folly and shame!)
Ibn al-Aʿrābī recited it. The hamza is for disapproval. al-ḥāfira originally is the road dug by travel, so calling it ḥāfira is a rational trope (majāz ʿaqlī), or it is in the sense of ascription, i.e. possessing digging; then it was used for every state you were in and then returned to. It is accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb, i.e. «shall I return ḥāfira», i.e. to my first way of youth and boyish love; or by removal of the preposition (nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. «shall I return to it». And al-ṣalaʿ is the receding of the hair of the forehead, and it mostly occurs in old age.
(الساهرة) The white, level land. It was named so because the mirage runs on it, from their saying ʿan sāhira [Translator's note: so in the source; probably «عين ساهرة», "a wakeful spring"] for flowing water, and for its opposite nāʾima (sleeping). Al-Ashʿath ibn Qays said:
وساهرة يضحي السراب مجللا ... لأقطارها قد جئتها متلثما
(Many a wakeful waste, whose sides the mirage comes to cover by forenoon, I have come to with my face veiled.)

* I'rab:
(وَالنَّازِعاتِ غَرْقاً، وَالنَّاشِطاتِ نَشْطاً، وَالسَّابِحاتِ سَبْحاً، فَالسَّابِقاتِ سَبْقاً، فَالْمُدَبِّراتِ أَمْراً) The wāw is the wāw of the oath. He, the Exalted, swore by the groups of angels that draw out the souls from the bodies. The answer to the oath by these things by which Allah swore is omitted, i.e. «by those that draw out, and so and so, you will surely be resurrected». As for غرقا, it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun) with omission of the added letters, meaning إغراقا, made accusative by what precedes it because it meets it in meaning, or by an omitted verb; or else as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. possessing thoroughness. Abū al-Baqāʾ's wording: «غرقا is a maṣdar according to the meaning, because the one who draws (al-nāziʿ) is the one who goes to the utmost in drawing the arrow or in pulling out the soul; and it is a maṣdar with the addition omitted, i.e. إغراقا.» And al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «He, Glorified is He, swore by the groups of angels that draw out the souls from the bodies», until he says: «غرقا: going to the utmost in drawing, i.e. they draw them out from the farthest reaches of the bodies.» And it is said النازعات are horses: He swore by the horses of the raiders, which strain at their reins with a straining in which the reins are pulled to the full because of the length of their necks, since they are pure Arabians. والناشطات نشطا is conjoined to والنازعات غرقا, and likewise His saying والسابحات سبحا. In al-Mukhtār: «al-sibāḥa, with kasra, is swimming; sabaḥa, yasbaḥu, with fatḥa; and al-sabḥ is free time; and al-sabḥ is also going about one's livelihood; and its pattern is qaṭaʿa and qatala.» فالسابقات سبقا is conjoined to what preceded, and likewise فالمدبرات أمرا. The fāʾ in both indicates their sequence without delay. أمرا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of المدبرات, and the answer of these oaths is omitted, as has preceded. (يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الرَّاجِفَةُ) يوم is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted answer; you may also attach it to what is indicated by His coming saying «قلوب يومئذ واجفة», i.e. on the day the quaking quakes, the hearts tremble. The clause ترجف الراجفة is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. (تَتْبَعُهَا الرَّادِفَةُ) The clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of الراجفة, i.e. it quakes, the follower following it; and الرادفة is the fāʿil (agent) of تتبعها. (قُلُوبٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ واجِفَةٌ أَبْصارُها خاشِعَةٌ) قلوب is a mubtadaʾ (subject); what licensed beginning with an indefinite noun is that it is qualified. يومئذ is an adverb annexed to its like, attached to واجفة; واجفة is a naʿt (adjective) of قلوب. أبصارها is a subject and خاشعة the khabar (predicate) of أبصارها, and the nominal clause is the predicate of قلوب. The eyes were annexed to the hearts with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. the eyes of their owners. (يَقُولُونَ أَإِنَّا لَمَرْدُودُونَ فِي الْحافِرَةِ) The clause is the predicate of an implied subject, i.e. they say. يقولون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and an agent. The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval, because they rejected the return and denied it. إنّ and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); مردودون is the predicate of إنّا; في الحافرة is attached to مردودون, and في means إلى, i.e. to the ḥāfira. It may also be attached to an omitted ḥāl, with «في» retaining its meaning, the meaning of الحافرة being the earth in which their graves are; and the meaning is: shall we be returned while we are in the ḥāfira? What follows is al-Rāghib's wording about al-ḥāfira: «His saying في الحافرة is a proverb for one who is returned whence he came, i.e. shall we be returned to life after we die? And it is said al-ḥāfira is the earth in which their graves are, and its meaning is: shall we be returned while we are in the ḥāfira, i.e. in the graves; and His saying في الحافرة on this view is in the position of a ḥāl. And it is said "so-and-so returned upon his ḥāfira", and "the old man returned to his ḥāfira", i.e. he became decrepit, as in His saying, the Exalted: ومنكم من يرد إلى أرذل العمر. And al-ḥāfira, it is said, is fāʿila in the sense of mafʿūla; and it is said it is by way of ascription, i.e. possessing digging, and what is meant is the earth; and the meaning is: shall we be returned in our graves alive? And it is said al-ḥāfira is the plural of ḥāfir in the sense of foot, i.e. shall we walk alive on our feet and tread the earth with them?» (أَإِذا كُنَّا عِظاماً نَخِرَةً) The interrogative is an emphasis of the content of the rejection and denial of the return, by relating it to a state incompatible with it. إذا is a future adverb, and what governs it is indicated by مردودون, i.e. when we are decayed bones, shall we be returned and resurrected, despite our being the farthest of things from life? (قالُوا تِلْكَ إِذاً كَرَّةٌ خاسِرَةٌ) A resumed statement presented to relate another disbelief branching from their previous disbelief. تلك is the subject, the reference being to the return and the restoration in the ḥāfira; إذا is a particle of answer and consequence with no governing effect, brought to convey emphasis of the losing return; كرة is the predicate of تلك and خاسرة an adjective of كرة. (فَإِنَّما هِيَ زَجْرَةٌ واحِدَةٌ) The fāʾ is connected with an omitted element whose meaning is: do not deem it hard, for it is only a single cry; meaning: do not think the return difficult for Allah the Exalted, for it is easy and light by His power, the Exalted. إنما is the restraining (kāffa) and the restrained (makfūfa); هي is the subject, زجرة the predicate and واحدة an adjective of زجرة, i.e. a single blast. The blast (al-nafḥa [Translator's note: so in the source, for al-nafkha]) was named a cry (zajra) because from it is understood a prohibition of holding back and lagging behind it. (فَإِذا هُمْ بِالسَّاهِرَةِ) The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, because it discloses an implied condition, i.e. so when it is blown...; إذا is of surprise (fujāʾiyya), and the discussion of it has preceded. هم is the subject and بالساهرة the predicate.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «يوم ترجف الراجفة» there is a predicative trope (majāz isnādī): He made the cause of the quaking a quaker. In al-Qurṭubī: «The origin of al-rajfa is movement; Allah the Exalted said: يوم ترجف الأرض. And al-rajfa here is not from movement only, but from their saying: the thunder rajafa, yarjufu, rajfan and rajīfan, i.e. it produced sound and movement; and from it the alarming rumours (al-arājīf) were named, because of the agitation of voices with them and people's plunging into them.»
2- And in His saying «تلك إذا كرة خاسرة» there is a predicative trope: He ascribed the loss to the return while its people are meant; the meaning is: if our return to the Resurrection is true, then that return is a losing return.
3- Likewise in His saying «فإذا هم بالساهرة» wakefulness was ascribed to the white land figuratively, just as they ascribed sleep to its opposite. Al-Ashʿath ibn Qays said:
وساهرة يضحي السراب مجللا ... لأقطارها قد جبتها متلثما
(Many a wakeful waste, whose sides the mirage comes to cover by forenoon, I have crossed with my face veiled.)
al-sāhira is the white land, because the mirage runs on it; it was described with wakefulness because the traveller in it is wakeful and does not sleep for fear of perishing, so it is a rational trope (majāz ʿaqlī). مجللا is the predicate of يضحي, i.e. covering its regions and sides. He says: many a desert which the day covers with a mirage resembling a horse's rope [Translator's note: so in the source («حبل الفرس»); possibly «جلّ الفرس», a horse-cloth, matching مجللا], I have come to wearing the face-veil for fear of the heat and the wind.

dervis-irab:15-26.t:
* I'rab:
(هَلْ أَتاكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسى) A resumptive utterance, intended to console the Messenger of Allah ﷺ over his people's denial of him. هل has the meaning of قد; it is also said to be a question of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī), the meaning being "Has the story of Moses not come to you?". أتاك: a past verb and a direct object; حديث موسى: the agent. (إِذْ ناداهُ رَبُّهُ بِالْوادِ الْمُقَدَّسِ طُوىً) إذ is an adverb of past time, attached to حديث موسى and not to أتاك as one might imagine, because their times differ; the clause ناداه is in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; ناداه: a past verb and a direct object; ربه: the agent; بالواد: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ناداه; the yāʾ of الوادي was dropped to follow the written form of the muṣḥaf; المقدس is an adjective of الوادي and طوى a badal (substitute); the discussion of it has been given at length before. It was read with tanwīn and without it. al-Jawharī said: «طوى is the name of a place in al-Shām; its ṭāʾ is pronounced with kasra or ḍamma; it is declined or diptote. Whoever declines it makes it the name of a valley and a place and makes it indefinite; whoever does not decline it makes it a town and a plot and makes it definite». (اذْهَبْ إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغى) The clause is the content of an omitted saying, its implied form being "and He said: Go"; it is also possible that it is a clause explicating the calling (nidāʾ). إلى فرعون: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to اذهب; إن with its noun, and the clause طغى is its khabar; the clause إنه طغى is a reason for the command to go. (فَقُلْ هَلْ لَكَ إِلى أَنْ تَزَكَّى) The fāʾ is a conjunction; قل an imperative verb whose agent is latent, the implied form being "you"; هل is an interrogative particle whose meaning is an offer (ʿarḍ), to invite him with gentleness, mildness and tactfulness; لك is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "inclination"; إلى أن تزكى: attached to the implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "Have you an inclination to purification?", like "Have you an inclination for good?", i.e. "Have you an inclination toward good?". The origin of تزكى is تتزكى, one of the two tāʾs having been dropped, i.e. you purify yourself from polytheism. The interrogative clause is the content of what is said; and أن and what follows are in the interpretation of a maṣdar, genitive through إلى, as has been given. (وَأَهْدِيَكَ إِلى رَبِّكَ فَتَخْشى) The wāw is a conjunction; أهديك is conjoined to تزكى, and the kāf is a direct object; إلى ربك: attached to أهديك; فتخشى is conjoined to أهديك. He made fear the goal of guidance because it is the pillar of the matter and the sum of piety; whenever a person fears his Lord, nothing issues from him but good. (فَأَراهُ الْآيَةَ الْكُبْرى) The fāʾ is a conjunction upon an omitted element, meaning "so he went, so he showed him"; أراه: «an imperfect verb» in the source [Translator's note: the verb is a past verb, not imperfect], its agent latent, the implied form being "he"; the hāʾ is the first object of أرى; الآية is the second object of أرى; الكبرى is an adjective of الآية, which is the turning of the staff into a serpent, or the hand. (فَكَذَّبَ وَعَصى) conjoined to what precedes. (ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ يَسْعى) ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay; it was used because the voiding and undoing of faith requires a long time; the clause يسعى is a ḥāl from the pronoun in أدبر. (فَحَشَرَ فَنادى فَقالَ: أَنَا رَبُّكُمُ الْأَعْلى) conjoined likewise; and the clause أنا ربكم الأعلى is the content of what is said. (فَأَخَذَهُ اللَّهُ نَكالَ الْآخِرَةِ وَالْأُولى) The fāʾ is a conjunction; أخذه الله: a past verb, a fronted direct object and a postponed agent; نكال الآخرة والأولى is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), a maṣdar of أخذ; the figurative usage is either in the verb, i.e. "He made an example of him by seizing, the example of the Hereafter and the first", or in the maṣdar, i.e. "He seized him with a seizing of exemplary punishment". It may also be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e. for the sake of making an example of him. al-Zamakhsharī confined himself to its being a confirming maṣdar; he said: «It is a confirming maṣdar, like وعد الله and صبغة الله, as if it were said: Allah made an example of him with the example of the Hereafter and the first». It is also possible that the accusative of نكال is by removal of the preposition, i.e. "with an example". al-Zajjāj preferred that it is a confirming maṣdar. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «نكل به ينكل, of the pattern qatala, نكلة قبيحة: he afflicted him with a calamity; and نكل به with tashdīd is intensive; the noun is النكال». الآخرة والأولى are two adjectives of the two words of Pharaoh. The last word is his saying «أنا ربكم الأعلى», and the first word is his saying before it «ما علمت لكم من إله غيري», and between the two words, as has been said, were forty years. (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِمَنْ يَخْشى) إن is a particle resembling the verb; في ذلك is the fronted khabar of إن; the lām is the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ) that gives emphasis; عبرة is the postponed noun of إن; لمن is an adjective of عبرة, and the clause يخشى is the ṣila of من.

dervis-irab:27-46.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سَمْكَها) its raising. One says سمك يسمك, of the pattern naṣara, the thing: he raised it; and one says "Allah raised the heaven (سمك الله السماء)". al-Farazdaq said:
إن الذي سمك السماء بنى لنا ... بيتا دعائمه أعزّ وأطول
(He who raised the heaven built for us a house whose pillars are mightier and taller.)
السمك is the maṣdar of سمك; it is also the ceiling, or the span from the top of the house to its bottom, and the stature of anything.
(فَسَوَّاها) He made it level and smooth, with no elevation or depression in it.
(وَأَغْطَشَ) In al-Qāmūs: «غطش the night, يغطش, of the pattern ḍaraba: it grew dark, like أغطش; and Allah أغطشه». al-Rāghib said: «Its origin is from الأغطش, the one with weak sight in his eye, and التغاطش is feigning blindness». One says أغطش الليل intransitively, like أظلم; so أفعل here is both transitive and intransitive.
(دَحاها) دحا the earth, يدحوها, دحوا, and دحى يدحى: i.e. he spread it and stretched it out; it is among the verbs with wāw and yāʾ (as the third radical), so it is written with alif and with yāʾ.

* I'rab:
(أَأَنْتُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقاً أَمِ السَّماءُ بَناها) The hamza is for a question of rebuke and reproach; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ, أشد a khabar and خلقا a tamyīz; أم is a conjunction and السماء is conjoined to أنتم; the clause بناها is a ḥāl, as if it were an explanation of the manner of its creation; it may be explicative, with no grammatical position; and it is also possible to parse السماء as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "stronger in creation". (رَفَعَ سَمْكَها فَسَوَّاها) The clause is a badal (substitute) of the clause بناها, following it; رفع سمكها: a past verb, a direct object and a latent agent, the implied form being "He", referring to Allah the Exalted; فسواها is conjoined to رفع. (وَأَغْطَشَ لَيْلَها وَأَخْرَجَ ضُحاها) conjoined to what precedes; ليلها is the object of أغطش and ضحاها the object of أخرج. (وَالْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ دَحاها) The wāw is a conjunction; الأرض is accusative by ishtighāl, by an omitted verb explained by what follows; بعد ذلك is an adverb attached to دحاها; and the clause دحاها is explicative. (أَخْرَجَ مِنْها ماءَها وَمَرْعاها) The clause is explicative of what is indispensable for the possibility of dwelling on it, namely arranging the matter of food and drink and the possibility of settling upon it; it may also be a ḥāl with an implied قد, i.e. "bringing forth", which is the view of most, although I incline to the first view. منها: attached to أخرج; ماءها a direct object and مرعاها conjoined to ماءها. المرعى here is a mīmī maṣdar with the sense of the passive. (وَالْجِبالَ أَرْساها) The wāw is a conjunction; الجبال is accusative by ishtighāl also, as before, and the clause is conjoined to the first. (مَتاعاً لَكُمْ وَلِأَنْعامِكُمْ) متاعا is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e. "He did that to provide enjoyment for you"; Zāda in his gloss on al-Bayḍāwī preferred that it be a maṣdar of its omitted verb indicated by the context, i.e. "We gave you enjoyment of it", which is not far-fetched; لكم is attached to متاعا; and ولأنعامكم is conjoined to لكم. (فَإِذا جاءَتِ الطَّامَّةُ الْكُبْرى) The fāʾ is a conjunction indicating that what follows depends on what precedes, as the word متاع suggests; إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition; the clause جاءت is in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; الطامة is the agent and الكبرى an adjective of الطامة. الطامة is the Resurrection. In al-Mukhtār: «A torrent came and طم the well, i.e. buried it and levelled it; and everything that became abundant until it rose and overcame has طم, of the pattern radda. One says "above every ṭāmma is a ṭāmma"; from it the Resurrection is called ṭāmma. الطم with kasra is dragging; one says "he came with الطم والرم", i.e. with abundant water». The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: «الطامة is the calamity that overwhelms (تطم على) calamities, i.e. rises above and overcomes them. Among their proverbs: "the valley ran and overflowed (طم على) the villages". It is the Resurrection because it overwhelms every terror; and it is said to be the second blast». The apodosis of إذا is omitted, indicated by the detail mentioned, the implied form being "there came of the momentous matters what does not cross the mind, no eye has seen, and no ear has heard".
(يَوْمَ يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنْسانُ ما سَعى) يوم is a badal (substitute) of إذا, a partial substitute (badal baʿḍ min kull); the clause يتذكر is in the position of genitive by annexation, and the returning pronoun is omitted, the implied form being "on which man remembers"; you may also make it an exact substitute (badal muṭābiq), the whole for the whole, meaning: when he sees his deeds recorded in his book he remembers them, having forgotten them. الإنسان is the agent of يتذكر, and ما is relative or maṣdarī. (وَبُرِّزَتِ الْجَحِيمُ لِمَنْ يَرى) conjoined to جاءت; برزت is a passive past verb and الجحيم a deputy agent; لمن: attached to برزت; and the clause يرى has no position, being a ṣila of من. (فَأَمَّا مَنْ طَغى وَآثَرَ الْحَياةَ الدُّنْيا فَإِنَّ الْجَحِيمَ هِيَ الْمَأْوى) The fāʾ is resumptive, and the utterance is resumptive, intended to explain the condition of people in this world; for this reason making the fāʾ the apodosis of إذا is weak and inadmissible. أما is a particle of condition and detail; من a relative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; the clause طغى has no position; آثر is conjoined to طغى; الحياة is a direct object and الدنيا an adjective of الحياة; the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis of أما; إن is a particle resembling the verb, الجحيم its noun, and هي a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; المأوى is the khabar of إن, and the clause is the khabar of من. The al in المأوى is a substitute for the pronoun referring to من; it is also said that the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "it is the abode for him"; the first is the view of the Kufans and the second the view of the Basrans. (وَأَمَّا مَنْ خافَ مَقامَ رَبِّهِ وَنَهَى النَّفْسَ عَنِ الْهَوى فَإِنَّ الْجَنَّةَ هِيَ الْمَأْوى) The clause is conjoined to the preceding clause. The wording of al-Rāzī: «These two attributes are the opposites of the two preceding attributes: His saying "But as for him who feared the standing before his Lord" is the opposite of His saying "As for him who transgressed", and His saying "and restrained the soul from desire" is the opposite of "and preferred the life of this world". As all ugly deeds are included in those two attributes, so all acts of obedience are included in these two.» (يَسْئَلُونَكَ عَنِ السَّاعَةِ أَيَّانَ مُرْساها) The clause is resumptive, intended to relate another kind of their obstinacy. يسألونك: an imperfect verb, an agent and a direct object; عن الساعة: attached to يسألونك; أيان is an interrogative noun, in the position of accusative as an adverb of time, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; مرساها is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and the nominal clause has no position, because it is an explanation of their question about the Hour, i.e. "when is its anchoring (irsāʾ)?", i.e. its establishing and fixing, or its end and resting-place, from the مرسى of the ship, which is where it arrives and where it settles. (فِيمَ أَنْتَ مِنْ ذِكْراها) فيم is a fronted khabar, and the dropping of the alif of the interrogative ما when preceded by a preposition has already been given; أنت is a postponed mubtadaʾ; من ذكراها is attached to what the khabar is attached to; the meaning is "in what part of its mention are you?"; the clause has no position, as if it were a denial and rejection of their question about the Hour and a statement of the falsity of the question. It is also said: فيم is a denial of their question, and what follows is a resumption giving the reason for the denial, i.e. "Why this question?", then a new start is made and it is said "you are of its mention (أنت من ذكراها)"; so فيم is not a fronted khabar of what follows but the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "Why this question that comes from the disbelievers?", and the speech is complete at that point in his view; then he resumes with the clause أنت من ذكراها as an explanation of the reason for the denial of their question, as if it were said: "It is near, not far, because you are one of its signs, so your being sent is enough evidence for them of its nearness and of the concern to prepare for it, so there is no sense in their asking about it". The meaning of أنت من ذكراها is "you are among its signs and reminders". (إِلى رَبِّكَ مُنْتَهاها) إلى ربك is a fronted khabar and منتهاها a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. (إِنَّما أَنْتَ مُنْذِرُ مَنْ يَخْشاها) إنما is restrictive (kāffa) and restricted (makfūfa); أنت is a mubtadaʾ, منذر a khabar and من a muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause يخشاها is the ṣila of من, with no position. (كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَها لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إِلَّا عَشِيَّةً أَوْ ضُحاها) كأن with its noun; يوم is an adverb of time attached to the sense of simile contained in كأن; the clause يرونها is in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; the clause لم يلبثوا is the khabar of كأنهم; إلا is a particle of restriction; عشية is an adverb of time attached to يلبثوا; أو is a conjunction; and ضحاها is conjoined to عشية. The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: «If you say: how is the annexation of الضحى to العشية sound? I say: because of the relation between them, since they meet in one day. If you say: why was it not said "except an evening or a forenoon", and what is the benefit of annexation? I say: to indicate that the duration of their stay seemed not to reach a whole day, but an hour of it, its evening or its forenoon; so when the day was left out, he annexed it to its evening. It is like His saying "they stayed only an hour of a day".»

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «أخرج منها ماءها ومرعاها» there is a loose trope (majāz mursal), because المرعى (pasture) is applied to what people eat, so المرعى was used for any food, of man and others; the relation is the use of the restricted for the unrestricted. It could also be an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), in that people's eating is likened to the grazing of beasts, and al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this, saying: «By مرعاها He meant what people and cattle eat; grazing was borrowed for man as roaming (الرتع) was borrowed in His saying "we shall roam and play".»
2- In His saying «فأما من طغى وآثر الحياة الدنيا فإن الجحيم هي المأوى وأما من خاف مقام ربه ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى» there is the art of antithesis (muqābala); the wording of al-Rāzī on this point has been given.
3- In His saying «أيان مرساها» there is an explicit metaphor, for he borrowed إرساء (anchoring), which is used only of what has weight.

farraa:1-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلنَّازِعَاتِ غَرْقاً﴾ to the end of the verses.
It is mentioned that they are the angels, and that the drawing out (النزع) is drawing the souls out of the breasts of the disbelievers. It is like your saying: والنازعات إغراقاً (by those who draw to the utmost), just as the archer draws the bow to the full (يُغرِق). Similar to it is: ﴿وَٱلنَّاشِطَاتِ نَشْطاً﴾. It is said that they take the soul of the believer as the hobble is loosened (يُنشَط) from the camel. What I have heard from the Arabs is that they say: أنشطتُ (I loosened), and "as though he had been loosened (أُنشِط) from a hobble"; and tying it is نشطها. So when you tie the rope on the camel's foreleg you are ناشط, and when you untie it you have أنشطته, and you are منشط.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلسَّابِحَاتِ سَبْحاً﴾.
The angels also; He made their descent from heaven like swimming. The Arabs say of the excellent horse [124/a]: إنه لسابح (it is a swimmer), when it passes stretching itself.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱلسَّابِقَاتِ سَبْقاً﴾.
They are the angels who outstrip the devils in bringing the revelation to the prophets, since the devils used to eavesdrop.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱلْمُدَبِّرَاتِ أَمْراً﴾.
They are the angels also; they descend with the lawful and the unlawful, and that is their arranging (تدبير) — though it belongs to Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He; but since they descended with it, they were called by that, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿نَزَلَ بِهِ الرُّوحُ الأَمِينُ﴾, and as He said: ﴿فَإِنَّهُ نَزَّلَهُ عَلَى قَلْبِكَ﴾, meaning: Gabriel, peace be upon him, brought it down upon the heart of Muhammad, may Allah bless them both and grant them peace, while it is Allah who sent it down. The questioner may ask: Where is the response (jawāb) to the oath in al-Nāziʿāt? It is one of those whose response is left out because the hearers know it. The meaning — as though, had it been overt, it would be: لتُبعثُنّ ولتُحاسَبُنّ (you will surely be resurrected and you will surely be called to account). What indicates that is their saying: "When we are decayed bones?" Do you not see that it is like a reply to His [implied] saying: "You will surely be resurrected", since they said: "When we are decayed bones, will we be resurrected?"

farraa:6-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ ٱلرَّاجِفَةُ﴾.
It is the first blowing [of the Trumpet]. ﴿تَتْبَعُهَا ٱلرَّادِفَةُ﴾: it is the second blowing.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلْحَافِرَةِ﴾.
It is said: [back] to our first state, to life. The Arabs say: أتيت فلاناً ثم رجعت على حافرتي (I came to So-and-so, then went back on my tracks), i.e. I returned to where I came from. Of that is the Arabs' saying: النقد عند الحافرة (payment at the very first moment). Its meaning: when he says "I have sold it to you", I come back to him with the price; and both are the same in meaning. Some say: النقد عند الحافر. He said: I asked one of the Arabs about it, and he said: النقد عند الحافر, meaning: at the hoof of the horse; as though this proverb arose concerning horses.
Some said: الحافرة is the ground in which their graves are dug, so He called it الحافرة, the meaning being المحفورة (the dug [ground]), just as it was said: ماء دافق (gushing water), meaning: مدفوق (poured out).

farraa:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿أَإِذَا كُنَّا عِظَاماً نَّاخِرَةً﴾. Al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to me from al-Suddī from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, who said: I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb reading: "إِذا كُنَّا عِظَاماً نَاخِرَةً". Al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: al-Kisāʾī narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl from ʿAṭāʾ from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān from ʿAlī, may Allah have mercy on him, that he read "نَخِرَةً"; and he claimed in this isnad of his that Ibn ʿAbbās read it "نخرة". [Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us], saying: Sharīk ibn ʿAbd Allāh and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Taymī Abū Saʿīd narrated to me from Mughīra from Mujāhid. Sharīk said: Ibn ʿAbbās read "عظاما ناخرة". Muḥammad said, with his isnad from Mughīra from Mujāhid: He said: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr saying on the pulpit: "What is the matter with boys who read (نخرة), when it is only (ناخرة)?" [Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us [124/b], saying: Mindal narrated to me from Layth from Mujāhid from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read: (ناخرة). The people of Medina and al-Ḥasan read: (نخرة). (ناخرة) is the better of the two ways in reading, because the verses [end] with alif. Do you not see that (ناخرة), alongside (الحافرة) and (الساهرة), is more in keeping with the way the Revelation comes? (الناخرة) and (النخرة) are the same in meaning, like الطامع and الطمِع, and الباخل and البخِل. Some exegetes distinguished between them and said: (النخرة) is the decayed [bone], and (الناخرة) is the hollow bone through which the wind passes and makes a whistling sound (ينخر).

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا هُم بِٱلسَّاهِرَةِ﴾.
It is the face of the earth. It is as though it was given this name because the living creatures have on it their sleeping and their waking (سهرهم). [Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us], saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Ḥibbān ibn ʿAlī narrated to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: (الساهرة) is the earth; and he recited:
ففيها لحمُ ساهرةٍ وبحرٍ * ومَا فاهوُا به لهمُ مُقِيمُ
(In it is the meat of land and sea, and what they have spoken of stays with them.)

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿طُوًى﴾.
It is a valley between Medina and Egypt. Whoever declines it as a triptote says: it is a masculine [name] with which we named a masculine thing, and this is the course of what is declined. Whoever does not decline it makes it diverted (maʿdūl) [125/a] from its [original] form, as one says: رأيت عمر وذفر [Translator's note: so in the source; read زفر] ومضر, which are not declined because they are diverted from their form, as though عمر was originally عامر, and زفر was زافر, and طوى was طاوٍ. We have not found any noun from [roots with] yāʾ and wāw that was diverted from its form other than طوى; so declining it is preferable to me, since I have not found a parallel to it in diversion.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿نَكَالَ ٱلآخِرَةِ وَٱلأُوْلَىٰ﴾.
One of the two utterances is his saying: ﴿مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُمْ مِّنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرِى﴾ and the other is his saying: ﴿أَنَا رَبُّكُم الأعْلَى﴾ (24).
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَأَخَذَهُ ٱللَّهُ نَكَالَ ٱلآخِرَةِ وَٱلأُوْلَىٰ﴾.
That is: Allah seized him with a seizing that was an exemplary punishment (nakāl) for the last and the first.

farraa:27-27.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿أَأَنتُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقاً أَمِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ﴾.
He means the people of Mecca. Then He described the sky and said: He built it.

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَغْطَشَ لَيْلَهَا﴾: He made its night dark.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَأَخْرَجَ ضُحَاهَا﴾: its light and its daytime.

farraa:30-30.t: His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَٱلأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ دَحَاهَا﴾. Putting الأرض in the accusative or the nominative is permissible; the accusative is more common in the reading of the readers. It is like His saying: ﴿وَالْقَمَرَ قَدَّرْنَاهُ مَنازِلَ﴾, along with many parallels in the Qurʾān.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَتَاعاً لَّكُمْ﴾.
He created that as a benefit for you and an enjoyment for you. If it had been متاعٌ لكم (nominative), it would be correct, as they said: ﴿لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إِلاَّ سَاعَةً مِّنْ نَهَارٍ بَلاَغٌ﴾, and as He said: ﴿مَتَاعٌ قَلِيلٌ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾; that is on resumption (istiʾnāf), with something implied for it that puts it in the nominative.

farraa:34-34.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا جَآءَتِ ٱلطَّآمَّةُ﴾.
It is the Resurrection, which overwhelms (تطمّ) everything. One says تَطِمّ and تطُمّ, two dialectal forms.

farraa:39-41.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ هِيَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ﴾.
The abode of those of this description. Likewise His saying: ﴿فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَنَّةَ هِيَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ﴾:
the abode of the one whom We have described with what We described him — fear of his Lord and his restraining [125/b] his soul from its desire.

farraa:42-42.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَيَّانَ مُرْسَاهَا﴾.
Someone may say: anchoring (الإرساء) belongs only to the ship, the mountains and the like; so how is the Hour described with anchoring? I said: it is like the ship which, when it was moving, came to anchor; and its anchoring is its standing (قيامها). Its standing is not like the standing of one who stands on his foot and the like; it is only like your saying: justice has been established (قام العدل) and truth has been established (قام الحق), i.e. it has appeared and become firm.

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُنذِرُ مَن يَخْشَاهَا﴾.
ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it in annexation (iḍāfa), while Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif and some of the people of Medina added tanwīn and said: "منذرٌ من يخشاها". Both are correct. It is like His saying: "بَالِغٌ أَمْرَه" and "بَالِغُ أمْرِه", and "مُوهِنٌ كَيْدَ الْكافِرِين" and ﴿موهنُ كيدِ الكَافرِينَ﴾, along with parallels to it in the Qurʾān.

farraa:46-46.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿إِلاَّ عَشِيَّةً أَوْ ضُحَاهَا﴾.
Someone may say: Does the evening (العشي) have a forenoon (ضحا)? The forenoon belongs only to the beginning of the day. This is clear and evident in the speech of the Arabs, that they say: آتيك العشيةَ أو غداتَها (I will come to you in the evening or its morning), and آتيك الغداةَ أو عشيتَها (I will come to you in the morning or its evening). العشية carries the meaning of "last" and الغداة the meaning of "first". One of Banū ʿUqayl recited to me:
نحن صبحنا عامراً فى دارها * عشية الهلال أو سَرارِها
(We attacked [the tribe of] ʿĀmir at dawn in their abode, on the evening of the new moon or of its last night.)
He meant: the evening of the new moon or the evening of the سَرار of the evening [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense is "the evening of its سرار", the last night of the month]. This is more forceful than آتيك الغداة أو عشيتها.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «النازعات»: the thing sworn by (muqsam bihi), attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied أقسم (I swear); «غرقا»: nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq (substitute for the absolute object), synonymous in meaning with its governing word «النازعات»; and the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam) is omitted, i.e.: لتبعثُنَّ (you will surely be raised).

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: «أمرا»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle «المدبِّرات».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The adverb «يوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied answer to the oath, i.e.: لتبعثُنَّ.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «تتبعها» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from {الرَّاجِفَةُ}.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: «قلوب» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «يومئذ»: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «واجفة»; and «واجفة» is a naʿt (adjective) of «قلوب», and it is what permits beginning with an indefinite noun.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: «أبصارها»: a second mubtadaʾ (subject), and «خاشعة»: the khabar (predicate) of the second mubtadaʾ; and the clause «أبصارها خاشعة» is the khabar of {قُلُوبٌ}.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «يقولون» is resumptive; the preposition «في الحافرة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مردودون».

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: «إذا»: adverbial and conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the meaning of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), its implied form being: "فهل نبعث؟" (will we then be raised?).

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The clause «قالوا» is resumptive; «إذًا»: a particle of reply.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The clause «فإنما هي زجرة» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The fāʾ is a conjunction; «إذا»: of surprise (fujāʾiyya); and the clause is conjoined to the clause «إنما هي زجرة».

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: (هل أتاك حديث موسى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: «إذ»: an adverbial noun, a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from {حَدِيثُ}; the preposition «بالواد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ناداه»; «طوى» is a badal.

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The clause «اذهب» is explicative of the calling; the clause «إنه طغى» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «فرعون».

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The preposition «لك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: سبيل (a way); and the genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of the implied mubtadaʾ, i.e.: is there a way existing for you to purification?

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «أهديك» is conjoined to the clause {تَزَكَّى}, and the clause «تخشى» is conjoined to the clause «أهديك».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «فأراه» is resumptive; «الآية» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The clause «فكذّب» is conjoined to the clause «أراه».

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The clause «فأخذه» is conjoined to the clause «قال»; «نكال»: nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq (substitute for the absolute object), synonymous in meaning with its governing word.

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The preposition «لمن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «عبرة».

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: «خلقا» is a tamyīz (specification); «أم» is a connected conjunction (muttaṣila); «السماء» is conjoined to «أنتم»; the clause «بناها» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The clause «رفع» is explicative of the building.

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: The wāw is resumptive; «الأرض» is the object of an omitted verb explained by what follows it, and the clause «دحاها» is explicative.

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: His saying «والجبال»: accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb explained by what follows it; the implied verb is conjoined to the clause «دحا», and the clause «أرساها» is explicative.

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: His saying «متاعا»: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); the preposition «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «متاعا».

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: The fāʾ is resumptive, and «إذا»: adverbial and conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the meaning of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the apodosis is His saying {فَأَمَّا مَنْ طَغَى}, as in: (إذا جاءك المحسنون فأمَّا مَنْ تزكَّى فادعُ له، وأما مَنْ ... ) (when the doers of good come to you, then as for one who has purified himself, pray for him, and as for one who …).

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: «يوم»: badal (substitute) of «إذا»; «ما» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and the interpreted maṣdar is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: (فأما من طغى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); «أما»: a particle of condition and detailing; «مَنْ»: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); «مَنْ» is not conditional, because a condition does not enter upon a condition.

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: (فإن الجحيم هي المأوى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The fāʾ is the linking one, and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «مَنْ», the link being implied (muqaddar), i.e.: مأواه (his refuge); and «هي» is for separation (faṣl).

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: (وأما من خاف مقام ربه) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined to the preceding «أمَّا» and what it entered upon; «مَنْ»: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject).

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: (فإن الجنة هي المأوى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is the khabar (predicate) of «مَنْ»; the fāʾ is the linking one; «هي» is for separation (faṣl); and the link is implied (muqaddar).

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: The clause «يسألونك» is resumptive, and the clause «أيان مرساها» is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from «الساعة»; «أيان» is an interrogative noun, an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); «مرساها» is the mubtadaʾ (subject).

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: The preposition «فيم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «أنت»; the preposition «مِنْ ذكراها» is attached to the khabar; the implied form is: "أنت كائن فيمَ مِنْ ذكراها؟", i.e.: you have nothing to do with mentioning it to them; and the clause «فيم أنت» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: (إلى ربك منتهاها) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: (إنما أنت منذر من يخشاها) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive; «مَنْ»: a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: The clause «كأنهم لم يلبثوا» is resumptive; «يوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «كأنهم»; the clause «لم يلبثوا» is the khabar (predicate) of «كأن»; «عشية»: an adverb attached to «يلبثوا»; and his saying «أو ضحاها», i.e.: the forenoon of the evening: he annexed the adverb to the pronoun of the other adverb by extension (ittisāʿan).

mekki-muskil:1-1.t:
His saying, the Exalted: (غرقا): a maṣdar (verbal noun), and likewise (نشطا), (سبحا) and (سبقا).
His saying (أمرا): a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (المدبرات). It is also said that it is a maṣdar; and also said that it is accusative by dropping the preposition, i.e. "by a command" (بأمر). Its being accusative by (المدبرات) is far-fetched only because the arranging (tadbīr) does not belong to the angels; it belongs only to Allah, exalted be His mention. They are sent with what Allah arranges and wills, and the arranging is not theirs, unless you construe it in the sense that they arrange it by Allah's command to them. The answer to the oath is omitted, its implied form being "By the Lord of these things mentioned, you will surely be resurrected"; what indicates this is their denial of the resurrection in His saying (يقولون أئنا لمردودون في الحافرة). It is also said that the answer is (إن في ذلك لعبرة). It is also said that its answer is (يوم ترجف), with the lām omitted, i.e. "surely on the day it quakes" (ليوم ترجف).

mekki-muskil:16-17.t: His saying (طوى اذهب): (طوى) is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from (الوادي). Whoever reads the ṭāʾ with kasra, which is the reading of al-Ḥasan, has it in the position of the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), like (ثنى), (عدى) and (سوى), its implied form being "in the sacred valley twice". Whoever does not decline it makes it deflected (maʿdūl) from (طاو), like ʿUmar and Zufar, and it is definite. Whoever declines it makes it like (حطم), not deflected. It is also said that it is a diptote only because it is the name of a spot of land and is definite.

mekki-muskil:25-25.t: His saying (نكال الآخرة): a maṣdar (verbal noun). It is also said that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

mekki-muskil:30-30.t: His saying (والأرض بعد ذلك): (الأرض) is accusative by an implied verb which (دحاها) explains. The nominative is permissible as a mubtadaʾ (subject). According to the Basrans the accusative is the preferred choice; al-Farrāʾ said that the nominative and the accusative are equal in it. Its like is (والجبال أرساها).

mekki-muskil:33-33.t: His saying (متاعا لكم ولأنعامكم): accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:37-37.t: His saying (فأما من طغى): (من) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is (فإن الجحيم) and what follows it. Its like is (وأما من خاف); but in the khabar a returning pronoun is omitted by which the khabar is completed; its implied form is "the Blaze is the refuge for him" and "the Garden is the refuge for him". It is also said that its implied form is "it is his refuge", and the alif and lām are a compensation for the omitted [pronoun].

mekki-muskil:42-42.t: His saying (أيان مرساها): (مرساها) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (أيان) is the khabar (predicate). It is an indeclinable (mabnī) adverbial meaning (متى) "when". It was made indeclinable only because it contains the meaning of the interrogative, which belongs to the particle; since it stood in the place of the particle and was used to ask a question, it was made indeclinable as the particle is; and it was made indeclinable on a vowel because the letter before the last is vowelless.

mekki-muskil:43-43.t: His saying (فيم أنت): the alif of (ما) was dropped as it was dropped from (عم) and the like; it is like it in reason and ruling, and it has already been mentioned.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿والنازعات﴾: the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, and «النازعات» is a noun in the genitive by the wāw of oath, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, i.e. "I swear"; the oath clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.
﴿غرقا﴾: standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), being synonymous with its governor ﴿النازعات﴾, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the answer to the oath is omitted, i.e. "you will surely be resurrected" (لنبعثن).

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿والناشطات﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «الناشطات» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ﴿النازعات﴾, genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra.
﴿نشطا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿والسابحات﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «السابحات» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ﴿النازعات﴾, genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra.
﴿سبحا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿فالسابقات﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction for sequence, and «السابقات» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ﴿النازعات﴾, genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra.
﴿سبقا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿فالمدبرات﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction for sequence and immediate succession, and «السابقات» [Translator's note: so in the source, carried over from the previous ayah; the word parsed here is «المدبرات»] is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ﴿النازعات﴾, genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra.
﴿أمرا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿يوم﴾: an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted answer to the oath.
﴿ترجف﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿الراجفة﴾: the fāʿil (agent) of «ترجف», nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma; the clause is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿تتبعها﴾: «تتبع» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma, and ﴿ها﴾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿الرادفة﴾: the fāʿil (agent) of «تتبع», nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma; the clause ﴿تتبعها الرادفة﴾ is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿الراجفة﴾.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿قلوب﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿يومئذ﴾: ﴿يوم﴾ is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿واجفة﴾; and ﴿إذٍ﴾ is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on a sukūn implied (muqaddar) because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of a genitive (majrūr), muḍāf ilayhi; the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being: "hearts trembling on the day when the quaking quakes, followed by the subsequent one".
﴿واجفة﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿قلوب﴾, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿أبصارها﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma; ﴿ها﴾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿خاشعة﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma; the clause ﴿خاشعة أبصارهم﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source, for «أبصارها خاشعة»] is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the first mubtadaʾ ﴿قلوب﴾.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿يقولون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent); the clause «يقولون» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "hum" (they), and the clause ﴿هم يقولون﴾ is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿أئنا﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative; «إن» is an abrogating, accusative-governing particle indeclinable on fatḥa, with no grammatical position; and ﴿نا﴾ is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of an accusative, the noun of «إن».
﴿لمردودون﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and «مردودون» is the khabar of «إن», nominative, the sign of its nominative being the wāw; the clause ﴿أئنا لمردودون﴾ is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿في﴾: a preposition.
﴿الحافرة﴾: a noun in the genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مردودون﴾.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿أئذا﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (al-istifhām al-inkārī), and «إذا» is an adverb (ẓarf) for future time, containing the meaning of condition, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of an accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what ﴿مردودون﴾ indicates, i.e. "we will be returned" (نرد).
﴿كنا﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb indeclinable on sukūn, and ﴿نا﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the noun of kāna [Translator's note: so in the source («خبر اسم كان»); ﴿نا﴾ is in fact the noun of kāna].
﴿عظاما﴾: the khabar of kāna, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿نخرة﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عظاما﴾, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the clause ﴿كنا﴾ is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it; and the apodosis of ﴿أئذا﴾ is omitted, indicated by ﴿مردودون﴾, i.e. "we will be returned".

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿قالوا﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma; the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent).
﴿تلك﴾: the tāʾ is a demonstrative indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject); the lām is for distance, and the kāf is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿إذًا﴾: a particle indeclinable on fatḥa, for answer and requital.
﴿كرة﴾: the khabar (predicate) of «تلك», nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿خاسرة﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿كرة﴾, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma; the clause ﴿قالوا﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿تلك إذًا كرة خاسرة﴾ is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿فإنما﴾: the fāʾ is a particle of resumption; «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, with no grammatical position; and «ما» restrains ﴿إن﴾ from its government (kāffa).
﴿هي﴾: a detached pronoun indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ), mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿زجرة﴾: the khabar (predicate) of «هي», nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿واحدة﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿زجرة﴾, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿فإذا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «إذا» is of surprise (fujāʾiyya).
﴿هم﴾: a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa [Translator's note: so in the source; «هم» ends in a sukūn], in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ), mubtadaʾ (subject); the mīm is the sign of the plural.
﴿بالساهرة﴾: the khabar (predicate) of ﴿هم﴾, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma [Translator's note: so in the source; ﴿بالساهرة﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar]; the clause is conjoined to the clause ﴿إنما هي زجرة واحدة﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿هل﴾: an interrogative particle indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, with no grammatical position.
﴿أتاك﴾: «أتى» is a past verb indeclinable on fatḥa, and the kāf is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿حديث﴾: the fāʿil (agent) of «أتى», nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma; it is muḍāf.
﴿موسى﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by a kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿إذ﴾: an adverb (ẓarf) for past time, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of an accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿حديث﴾.
﴿ناداه﴾: «نادى» is a past verb indeclinable on fatḥa, and the hāʾ is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ربه﴾: «رب» is the fāʿil (agent) of «نادى», nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma; it is muḍāf, and the hāʾ is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿بالواد﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition indeclinable on kasra, and ﴿الواد﴾ is a noun in the genitive, the sign of the genitive being a kasra implied (muqaddar) on the elided yāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿ناداه﴾.
﴿المقدس﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿الوادي﴾, genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra.
﴿طوى﴾: a badal (substitute) from «الوادي», genitive by a kasra implied on the alif; the clause ﴿ناداه﴾ is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿اذهب﴾: an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "anta" (you).
﴿إلى﴾: a preposition indeclinable on sukūn.
﴿فرعون﴾: a noun in the genitive, the sign of its genitive being the fatḥa, because it is a diptote; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اذهب﴾.
﴿إنه﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), indeclinable on fatḥa, with no grammatical position, and the hāʾ is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of an accusative, the noun of ﴿إن﴾.
﴿طغى﴾: a past verb indeclinable on fatḥa; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he), referring back to Pharaoh; the clause ﴿طغى﴾ is in the position of a nominative, the khabar (predicate) of «إن», and the clause ﴿اذهب﴾ is in the position of an accusative, the content of an omitted saying.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿فقل﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, and «قل» is an imperative verb indeclinable on sukūn; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "anta" (you); the clause ﴿قل﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿اذهب﴾.
﴿هل﴾: an interrogative particle indeclinable on sukūn, with no grammatical position.
﴿لك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "a desire existing for you"; the interrogative clause is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿إلى﴾: a preposition.
﴿أن﴾: a maṣdar-forming, accusative-governing particle, indeclinable on sukūn.
﴿تزكى﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being a fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "anta" (you); the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أن تزكى﴾ is in the genitive by ﴿إلى﴾, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted «رغبة» (desire).

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿وأهديك﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «أهديك» is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa, conjoined to ﴿تزكى﴾; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being ﴿أنا﴾ (I); and the kāf is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿إلى﴾: a preposition indeclinable on sukūn.
﴿ربك﴾: «رب» is a noun in the genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; it is muḍāf, and the kāf is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أهديك﴾.
﴿فتخشى﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; [«تخشى» is] an imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa, conjoined to ﴿تزكى﴾; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "anta" (you).

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿فأراه﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «أراه» is a past verb; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he); and the hāʾ is a pronoun in the position of an accusative, the first object of ﴿أرى﴾.
﴿الآية﴾: the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿أرى﴾.
﴿الكبرى﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿الآية﴾, accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿فكذب﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «كذب» is a past verb; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being ﴿هو﴾ (he).
