﴿وعصى﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «كذب» [Translator's note: so in the source, carried over from the line above; the verb parsed here is «عصى»] is a past verb; its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he); the two clauses ﴿كذب﴾ and ﴿عصى﴾ are conjoined to ﴿أُراه﴾.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction.
﴿أدبر﴾: a past verb; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he); the clause ﴿أدبر﴾ is conjoined to ﴿عصى﴾.
﴿يسعى﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he); the clause ﴿يسعى﴾ is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in ﴿أدبر﴾.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿فحشر﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «حشر» is a past verb; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he).
﴿فنادى﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «نادى» is a past verb; its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he); the clause ﴿فحشر﴾ is conjoined to ﴿أدبر﴾, and the clause ﴿فنادى﴾ is conjoined to ﴿فحشر﴾.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿فقال﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «قال» is a past verb; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he); the clause ﴿فقال﴾ is conjoined to ﴿فنادى﴾.
﴿أنا﴾: a pronoun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ), mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿ربكم﴾: «رب» is the khabar (predicate), and the pronoun is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿الأعلى﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿رب﴾, nominative; the clause ﴿أنا ربكم﴾ is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿فأخذه﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «أخذ» is a past verb; the hāʾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of an accusative, a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿أخذه﴾ is conjoined to ﴿قال﴾.
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿نكال﴾: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative (manṣūb).
﴿الآخرة﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
﴿والأولى﴾: conjoined to «الآخرة», genitive by an implied (muqaddar) kasra.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh).
﴿في﴾: a preposition.
﴿ذلك﴾: a demonstrative in the position of a genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of a nominative, the fronted khabar (predicate) of «إن».
﴿لعبرة﴾: the lām is the emphasising lām of ibtidāʾ, and «عبرة» is the postponed noun of «إن».
﴿لمن﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عبرة﴾.
﴿يخشى﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he); the clause ﴿يخشى﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿أأنتم﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of reproach (al-istifhām al-tawbīkhī), and «أنتم» is mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أشد﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿خلقا﴾: tamyīz (specification), accusative (manṣūb).
﴿أم﴾: a conjunction.
﴿السماء﴾: a noun conjoined to ﴿أنتم﴾, nominative.
﴿بناها﴾: «بنى» is a past verb; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (He); ﴿ها﴾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿بناها﴾ is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿رفع﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (He).
﴿سمكها﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and the pronoun is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿فسواها﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «سواها» is a past verb indeclinable on fatḥa; its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (He); and the pronoun is in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿رفع﴾ is a badal (substitute) from the clause ﴿بناها﴾, and the clause ﴿سواها﴾ is conjoined to ﴿رفع﴾.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿وأغطش﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (He).
﴿ليلها﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and the pronoun is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿وأخرج﴾: a past verb indeclinable on fatḥa; its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (He).
﴿ضحاها﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and the pronoun is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; the two clauses ﴿أغطش﴾ and ﴿أخرج﴾ are conjoined to ﴿رفع﴾.

muyesser-irab:30-30.t:
﴿والأرض﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «الأرض» is accusative (manṣūb) by preoccupation (ʿalā al-ishtighāl), by an omitted verb indicated by what follows it.
﴿بعد﴾: an adverb (ẓarf), attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿دحاها﴾.
﴿ذلك﴾: a demonstrative in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿دحاها﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (He); and the pronoun is in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause ﴿دحاها﴾ is explicative (tafsīriyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:31-31.t:
﴿أخرج﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (He).
﴿منها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أخرج﴾.
﴿ماءها﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and the pronoun is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿ومرعاها﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «مرعى» is a noun conjoined to ﴿ماءها﴾, and the pronoun is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi. The clause ﴿أخرج...﴾ explains His saying ﴿دحاها﴾, so it has no grammatical position; or it is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الأرض», with «قد» implied.

muyesser-irab:32-32.t:
﴿والجبال﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «الجبال» is accusative (manṣūb) by preoccupation (ʿalā al-ishtighāl), by an omitted verb indicated by what follows it.
﴿أرساها﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (He); and the pronoun is in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause ﴿أرساها﴾ is explicative (tafsīriyya), with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿الجبال أرساها﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿الأرض بعد ذلك دحاها﴾.

muyesser-irab:33-33.t:
﴿متاعا﴾: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative (manṣūb); or standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, because it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), the implied form being: "He gives you provision".
﴿لكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿متاعا﴾.
﴿ولأنعامكم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and the lām is a preposition; «أنعامكم» is a noun in the genitive, and the pronoun is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿لأنعامكم﴾ is conjoined to ﴿لكم﴾.

muyesser-irab:34-34.t:
﴿فإذا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «إذا» is an adverb (ẓarf) for future time, containing the meaning of condition.
﴿جاءت﴾: a past verb, the tāʾ being for the feminine; the clause ﴿جاءت﴾ is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it.
﴿الطامة﴾: the fāʿil (agent) of «جاءت», nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿الكبرى﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿الطامة﴾, nominative.

muyesser-irab:35-35.t:
﴿يوم﴾: «يوم» is a badal (substitute) from ﴿إذا﴾, accusative (manṣūb).
﴿يتذكر﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); the clause «يتذكر» is in the position of a genitive by being put in construct.
﴿الإنسان﴾: the fāʿil (agent) of «يتذكر», nominative.
﴿ما﴾: maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya).
﴿سعى﴾: a past verb; the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿ما سعى﴾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:36-36.t:
﴿وبرزت﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; [«برزت» is] a past verb, passive (built for that whose agent is not named); ﴿برزت﴾ is conjoined to ﴿جاءت﴾.
﴿الجحيم﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿لمن﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿برزت﴾.
﴿يرى﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative.

muyesser-irab:37-37.t:
﴿فأما﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; «أما» is a particle of condition and detailing.
﴿من﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿طغى﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he); the clause ﴿طغى﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:38-38.t:
﴿وآثر﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he); ﴿آثر﴾ is conjoined to ﴿طغى﴾.
﴿الحياة﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb).
﴿الدنيا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿الحياة﴾, accusative.

muyesser-irab:39-39.t:
﴿فإن﴾: the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis of ﴿أما﴾, and «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh).
﴿الجحيم﴾: the noun of «إن», accusative (manṣūb).
﴿هي﴾: a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl).
﴿المأوى﴾: the khabar (predicate) of «إن», nominative (marfūʿ); the clause is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of ﴿من﴾.

muyesser-irab:40-40.t:
﴿وأما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «أما» is a particle of condition and detailing.
﴿من﴾: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿خاف﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he); the clause ﴿من خاف﴾ is conjoined to ﴿من طغى﴾, and the clause ﴿خاف﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿مقام﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb).
﴿ربه﴾: «رب» is muḍāf ilayhi, and the pronoun is also muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿ونهى﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; [«نهى» is] a past verb indeclinable on fatḥa; its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he); the clause ﴿ونهى﴾ is conjoined to ﴿خاف﴾.
﴿النفس﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
﴿عن﴾: a preposition indeclinable on sukūn.
﴿الهوى﴾: a noun in the genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra [Translator's note: so in the source; on «الهوى» the kasra is implied on the alif]; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نهى﴾.

muyesser-irab:41-41.t:
﴿فإن﴾: the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis of ﴿أما﴾, and «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh).
﴿الجنة﴾: the noun of «إن», accusative (manṣūb).
﴿هي﴾: a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl).
﴿المأوى﴾: the khabar (predicate) of «إن», nominative (marfūʿ); the clause is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of ﴿من﴾.

muyesser-irab:42-42.t:
﴿يسألونك﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil (agent), and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿عن﴾: a preposition indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn.
﴿الساعة﴾: a noun in the genitive (majrūr).
﴿أيان﴾: an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative as an adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿مرساها﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the pronoun ﴿ها﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi. The clause ﴿أيان مرساها﴾ is explicative (tafsīriyya), with no grammatical position; or it is in the position of an accusative by an omitted saying indicated by the verb ﴿يسألونك﴾, the implied form being: ﴿يقولون أيان مرساها﴾ ("they say: when is its arrival?").

muyesser-irab:43-43.t:
﴿فيم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿أنت﴾: a pronoun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ), a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿من﴾: a preposition indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn.
﴿ذكراها﴾: a noun in the genitive, and the pronoun is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to that to which the khabar is attached; the clause has no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:44-44.t:
﴿إلى﴾: an indeclinable (mabnī) preposition.
﴿ربك﴾: «رب» is a noun in the genitive, and the pronoun is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of a nominative, khabar (predicate).
﴿منتهاها﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the pronoun is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:45-45.t:
﴿إنما﴾: [«إنّ»] restrained by the restraining «ما» (kāffa wa-makfūfa).
﴿أنت﴾: a pronoun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ), mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿منذر﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative.
﴿من﴾: a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿يخشاها﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, and ﴿ها﴾ is a pronoun in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿يخشاها﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿من﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:46-46.t:
﴿كأنهم﴾: «كأن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿هم﴾ is its noun.
﴿يوم﴾: «يوم» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative (manṣūb).
﴿يرونها﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil (agent), and ﴿ها﴾ is a pronoun in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of a genitive.
﴿لم﴾: a particle of negation, conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning], and jussive.
﴿يلبثوا﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative [Translator's note: so in the source; after «لم» the verb is jussive (majzūm), the sign being the elision of the nūn], and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿لم يلبثوا﴾ is in the position of a nominative, the khabar (predicate) of «كأن».
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿عشية﴾: an adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يلبثوا﴾.
﴿أو﴾: a conjunction.
﴿ضحاها﴾: conjoined to «عشية», accusative by an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa, and the pronoun is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: وَالنَّازِعاتِ is genitive by the wāw of oath; it was also said that the implied form is "by the Lord of النازعات". Shuʿba related from Sulaymān, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, concerning «النازعات»: he said: the angels. And Shuʿba related from al-Suddī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning وَالنَّازِعاتِ: he said: [the angel] draws out his soul. So the implied form becomes "by the angels who draw out". غَرْقاً is a maṣdar (verbal noun). Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: their souls are drawn out, then drowned, then burnt, then cast into the Fire. The implied form is "by the Lord of النازعات", and the meaning is: the souls are drowned, drowning thoroughly (فتغرق غرقا), [as in] وَاللَّهُ أَنْبَتَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ نَباتاً [Nūḥ: 17]. [Translator's note: i.e. the maṣdar follows a verb implied by the context, as نباتا follows أنبت rather than its own verb.]

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: يَقُولُونَ, i.e. in this world. أَإِنَّا لَمَرْدُودُونَ فِي الْحافِرَةِ: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning فِي الْحافِرَةِ: he said: He is saying "into life". Ibn Zayd said: into the Fire. Mujāhid said: into the earth. On Mujāhid's view the implied form is "into the dug earth (المحفورة)", i.e. into the grave, like مِنْ ماءٍ دافِقٍ [al-Ṭāriq: 6], i.e. poured out (مدفوق); its true sense in Arabic is "of water possessing gushing". On the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, فِي الْحافِرَةِ [means]: we will live as we lived the first time.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: [The reading «ناخرة»] is soundly established from Ibn ʿAbbās — Ibn ʿUyayna related it from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār from Ibn ʿAbbās — and soundly established from Ibn al-Zubayr, and related from ʿUmar and Ibn Masʿūd; these are four of the Companions. In addition it is the reading of Ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī, and it is more in keeping with the verse-endings before and after it. The reading نَخِرَةً is that of the people of the two Sanctuaries, al-Ḥasan and Abū ʿAmr. Both readings are good, because the majority transmitted them.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: It was said: the meaning is a return and a coming back, and they made it a losing one because they had been promised the Fire in it.

nahhas-irab:13-14.t: فَإِذا هُمْ بِالسَّاهِرَةِ (14): Sufyān said: الساهرة is a land in Syria. Saʿīd related from Qatāda: الساهرة is Hell. Abū Jaʿfar said: الساهرة in the speech of the Arabs is the wide, fearsome land in which one stays awake out of fear. Abū Ḥātim claimed that the implied form is "then behold, they are at الساهرة — by النازعات". This is a clear mistake, because one does not begin with the fāʾ, and النازعات is at the start of the surah. This is the fourth view on the answer to the oath.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: هَلْ may be in the sense of «قد»; the lexicographers have reported that. It may also have its usual meaning.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t:
طُوىً with nunation (tanwīn) and ḍamma on the ṭāʾ is the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī. The reading of the people of Medina and Abū ʿAmr is without nunation and with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ. The reading of al-Ḥasan is طِوىً with kasra on the ṭāʾ and nunation; its meaning in his view is "in the valley that was hallowed twice and in which [Moses] was called". The reading with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ and nunation is on the basis that it is a name of the valley and not a deflected form (maʿdūl); it is just like your saying حطم, therefore it is declined as a triptote. Whoever does not decline it makes it deflected, like عمر. But al-Farrāʾ rejects that, because he claimed that he does not know in the speech of the Arabs any noun from roots with yāʾ or wāw that is deflected from فاعل to فُعَل. Abū Jaʿfar said: It is possible that the non-declension is on the basis that it is a name of the spot (البقعة), so it would be other than what he interpreted. It has been read without nunation by those whose word constitutes proof.
اذْهَبْ إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغى (17): whoever says يطغى in the imperfect says طغيت, and it is الطغيان; whoever says يطغو says طغوت.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: The reading of the people of Medina and the reading of Abū ʿAmr is تَزَّكَّى [with doubled zāy], and [the others read] تَزَكَّى with the zāy undoubled; the meaning and the implied form in Arabic are one, because the original of تزكى is تتزكى, and one tāʾ was omitted. Whoever says تزّكّى assimilated it (idghām). No difference between them is known. [Translator's note: the source says «قراءة أهل المدينة وقراءة أبي عمرو تَزَكَّى بتخفيف الزاي», which appears to have lost a word; Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr are known to read with the doubled zāy. The bracketed additions follow the logic of the explanation.] Ibn Zayd said: «تزكّى» means "to submit (become Muslim)"; he said: every تزكية in the Qur'an is Islam.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: وَأَهْدِيَكَ إِلى رَبِّكَ is conjoined, and likewise فَتَخْشى, i.e. so that you fear His punishment by abandoning disobedience to Him.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: وَالنَّاشِطاتِ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to النازعات, i.e. those who pull out the spirits swiftly; one says نشطه when he pulled it swiftly. However, al-Farrāʾ reported نشطه in the sense of "he tied it", and أنشطه "he untied it", and it is reported from the Arabs: كأنما أنشط من عقال ("as though he were released from a hobble"). He was contradicted in this, and the one who contradicted him cited as evidence the poet's saying: [al-rajaz] 536- أضحت همومي تنشط المناشطا (My cares have come to pull me in every direction.)

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: [الْآيَةَ الْكُبْرى] is among the [expressions] from which the alif and lām may not be omitted, nor may it be brought in the indefinite. [Translator's note: the source does not name the word discussed; الكبرى, an elative (afʿal) feminine form, is presumably meant.]

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: The meaning of the fāʾ is that it indicates that the second comes after the first, while the wāw is for combination. This is their basic meaning.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: In the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:23-24.t: فَحَشَرَ: the object is omitted, i.e. "and he gathered his people", as Ibn Zayd said: he gathered his people, فَنادى among them فَقالَ أَنَا رَبُّكُمُ الْأَعْلى (24).

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: Al-Farrāʾ said: That is, Allah seized him with a seizing as an exemplary punishment (نكالا) for the last and the first.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: That is, [for one who] fears Allah's punishment, as it befell someone else when he disobeyed.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: أَأَنْتُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقاً أَمِ السَّماءُ: that is, why do you deny the resurrection when the creation of the heaven is harder than your resurrection?

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: That is, as a roof for the earth.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: وَأَغْطَشَ لَيْلَها: a figurative annexation (iḍāfa majāz), because the meaning of night is the departure of the sun; since it sets in the sky, "its night" was said, as one says "the riding animal's saddle". Likewise وَأَخْرَجَ ضُحاها.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: It is conjoined (maʿṭūf), i.e. "and by the angels who glide (السابحات)", meaning the swift ones. ʿAṭāʾ said: السَّابِحاتِ are the ships. سَبْحاً is a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:30-30.t:
وَالْأَرْضَ is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "and He spread out the earth". Al-Farrāʾ claimed ] [Translator's note: a stray bracket appears here in the source.] that the accusative and the nominative are both permissible, and that it is like وَالْقَمَرَ قَدَّرْناهُ مَنازِلَ [Yā Sīn: 39], meaning in [allowing] the nominative and the accusative.
Abū Jaʿfar said: There is a difference between them, because in His saying الْقَمَرَ قَدَّرْناهُ مَنازِلَ the nominative is good, since its implied form is "and a sign for them is the moon". In وَالْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ دَحاها (30) the nominative is remote, because before it is something a verb has governed, and it is not connected to anything in the nominative. This is a clear difference. We know of no one who read «والأرض» in the nominative, whereas «والقمر» in the nominative was read by the leading readers.
There is a difficulty in the verse, because He, the Exalted, said: قُلْ أَإِنَّكُمْ لَتَكْفُرُونَ بِالَّذِي خَلَقَ الْأَرْضَ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ [Fuṣṣilat: 9], and after it ثُمَّ اسْتَوى إِلَى السَّماءِ, which indicates that the creation of the heaven came after the creation of the earth, while here [He says] وَالْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ دَحاها (30). Among the soundest and best things said about this is what Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, created the earth before the heaven and measured out its provisions in it, but did not spread it out; then He created the heaven, then spread out the earth after it. Mujāhid and al-Suddī said: وَالْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ دَحاها means "together with that He spread it out", as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: عُتُلٍّ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ زَنِيمٍ [al-Qalam: 13]. Abū Jaʿfar said: The first view is preferable, so that the word keeps its usual meaning. The meaning of الدّحو in the language is spreading out; one says دحوت أدحو and دحيت أدحي, and from the second [form] the name دحية was given.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: [وَالْجِبالَ is accusative] by an implied verb as well.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: Al-Farrāʾ said: That is, He created that as a benefit and enjoyment for you. He said: The nominative is also permissible, like مَتاعٌ قَلِيلٌ [Āl ʿImrān: 197].

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: [الطَّامَّةُ is] the Resurrection; Allah magnified its matter and warned of it. Abū Jaʿfar said: When the Arabs magnify something, they describe it as الطامة (the overwhelming).

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: That is, when he reads his record and sees his place, he remembers his deeds.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: He made الجحيم feminine because of the meaning "the Fire"; it is an epithet (naʿt) of it here.

nahhas-irab:37-39.t: مَنْ is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is فَإِنَّ الْجَحِيمَ هِيَ الْمَأْوى (39). The implied form according to the Kufans is "then it is his abode (مأواه)", the alif [and lām] being a substitute for the pronoun; the implied form according to the Basrans is "it is the abode for him".

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: فَالسَّابِقاتِ سَبْقاً (4) فَالسَّابِقاتِ is conjoined (maʿṭūf), i.e. "and by the angels who outstrip the devils with the revelation". ʿAṭāʾ said: السابقات are the horses. سَبْقاً is a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خافَ مَقامَ رَبِّهِ: i.e. the standing of the reckoning for his sins. وَنَهَى النَّفْسَ عَنِ الْهَوى: [الهوى] is inclination towards what is not good.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: Al-Farrāʾ said: It may be said: anchoring (الإرساء) belongs only to the ship, the mountains and the like, so how is the Hour described with anchoring? The answer is that it is like the ship when it sails and then comes to anchor; its anchoring is its standing (قيامها), and that is not like the standing of one who stands on his feet and the like, but as you say: قام العدل ("justice was established"), قام الحقّ ("the truth was established"), i.e. it appeared and became firm.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: That is, mentioning it is not your concern, because you do not know its time. The original is «في ما»; the alif was omitted to distinguish between the interrogative and the informative, since before ما there is a particle that puts it in the genitive. Pausing on it is فيمه, nothing else being permissible, so that the alif and the vowel of the mīm are not both lost. The correct thing is not to pause on it, so as not to differ from the written text (السواد) by adding the hāʾ, or to commit a solecism if one pauses on it without the hāʾ.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: In the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. the ultimate knowledge of it.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn Muḥayṣin and Ṭalḥa read مُنْذِرٌ مَنْ يَخْشاها with nunation (tanwīn); this is the original, and it is only omitted for lightness. [Translator's note: the source prints the phrase as «مُنْذِرُ مَنْ يَخْشاها» without the tanwīn sign, although it describes the nunated reading.]

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: That is, what they were in has passed away from them, so they do not think about what has gone and it seems little to them. In this there is a sense of warning to whoever is deluded by this world and his safety in it, that he will leave it shortly, and the pleasure and joy he found in it will leave him, as though he had remained in it only an evening or its morning.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
فَالْمُدَبِّراتِ is conjoined, i.e. "and by the angels". He said: There is no disagreement among the people of knowledge about this, that the angels are meant by it, and it is figurative (majāz), because Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, is the One who arranges (al-mudabbir) all things. He said: يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ مِنَ السَّماءِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ [al-Sajda: 5]. Since the angels, Allah's blessings be upon them, descend with the revelation, the rulings and the dispensing of the rains, they were called مدبرات figuratively. Al-Farrāʾ said: It is as He said: فَإِنَّهُ نَزَّلَهُ عَلى قَلْبِكَ [al-Baqara: 97], ascribing the sending down to Jibrāʾīl, peace be upon him, while it is Allah who sent it down; and likewise نَزَلَ بِهِ الرُّوحُ الْأَمِينُ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 193]. أَمْراً is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). It is also possible that the implied form is "those who arrange by a command from Allah", the bāʾ being omitted so that the verb passes on directly; Sībawayh recited: [al-basīṭ] 537-
أمرتك الخير فافعل ما أمرت به ... فقد تركتك ذا مال وذا نشب
(I commanded you to do good, so do what you were commanded, for I have left you possessed of wealth and property.)
As for the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), there are four views about it. The soundest and best of them is that it is omitted, something clearly indicating it; the meaning is "by النازعات, you will surely be resurrected", and they said: "Shall we be resurrected when we are decayed bones?" Their saying أَإِذا كُنَّا indicates that omitted [answer]. It was said [secondly]: the answer is إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِمَنْ يَخْشى (26); this is far-fetched, because what lies between them is very distant. It was said [thirdly]: only the lām was omitted, the implied form being "on the day the quaking quakes" (ليوم ترجف الراجفة). This too is even more far-fetched than that, because the lām is not among the things that are omitted, since it occurs on most things, so one would not know where it was omitted from; and if its omission were permissible, والله زيد منطلق would be permissible in the sense [of having] the lām. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: الرَّاجِفَةُ is the first blast, and الرَّادِفَةُ is the second. Abū Hurayra related from the Prophet ﷺ: between them are forty.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: A mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). ʿAṭāʾ said: واجفة means moving; someone else said: fearful.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: A mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); [the meaning is] that they are abased because of their disgrace on the Day of Resurrection for their sins. The statement is complete here.

safi-cedvel:1-5.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear". (غرقا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, since it meets it in meaning [Note: Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "النازع is the one who pulls deeply (al-mughriq) when drawing the arrow or the soul; it is a maṣdar with the augment deleted, i.e. إغراقا. It is also permissible that it be a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. 'possessors of deep pulling'."]. (الواو) is a conjunction in both places, and likewise (الفاء) in both places. (أمرا) a direct object of the active participle on المدبّرات.
Clause: « (أقسم) بالنازعات ... » has no grammatical position; it is an initial clause ... and the answer to the oath is omitted, its implied form being "you will surely be resurrected, O disbelievers".

* Morphology:
(النازعات): plural of النازعة, feminine of النازع, an active participle from the triliteral نزع; its wazn is فاعل; النازعات are the angels.
(الناشطات): plural of الناشطة, feminine of الناشط, an active participle from the triliteral نشط; its wazn is فاعل; الناشطات are the angels.
(السابحات): plural of السابحة, feminine of السابح, an active participle from the triliteral سبح; its wazn is فاعل; السابحات are the angels.
(السابقات): plural of السابقة, feminine of السابق, an active participle from the triliteral سبق; its wazn is فاعل; السابقات are the angels.
(المدبّرات): plural of المدبّرة, feminine of المدبّر, an active participle from the quadriliteral دبّر; its wazn is مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(غرقا): a samāʿī maṣdar of the verb غرق, bāb naṣara; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn..
Or it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) of (أغرق).
(نشطا): a samāʿī maṣdar of the verb نشط, bāb ḍaraba; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn..
(سبقا): a samāʿī maṣdar of the verb سبق, bāb ḍaraba; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn..

safi-cedvel:6-11.t:
* I'rab:
(يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to the verb implied in لتبعثنّ. (قلوب) a mubtadaʾ, nominative, whose khabar is the clause أبصارها خاشعة. (يومئذ) an adverb, accusative – or indeclinable on fatḥa because it is annexed to the indeclinable إذ – attached to (واجفة) [Note: or it is a badal from يوم ترجف]. (واجفة) an adjective of قلوب [Note: separating the adjective from the described noun by an intervening element was permissible because it is an adverb], nominative. (أبصارها) a second mubtadaʾ, nominative, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the eyes of their owners".. its khabar is (خاشعة)..
Clause: «ترجف الراجفة ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «تتبعها الرادفة ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from الراجفة.
And the clause: «قلوب ... أبصارها خاشعة» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «أبصارها خاشعة» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (قلوب).
10- 11 (الهمزة) for interrogation of denial. (اللام) for emphasis, and it is the shifted lām (al-muzaḥlaqa). (في الحافرة) attached to (مردودون). (الهمزة) like the first. (إذا) an indeclinable adverb in the position of accusative, attached to the content of the apodosis..
And the clause: «يقولون ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هم" (they)..
And the nominal clause is a ḥāl from the possessors of the throbbing hearts [Note: It is permissible that the clause يقولون be an explanatory resumption].
And the clause: «إنّا لمردودون ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
And the clause: «كنّا عظاما ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.. and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "then shall we be raised anew?".

* Morphology:
(6) الراجفة: feminine of الراجف, an active participle from the triliteral رجف; its wazn is فاعل.
(7) الرادفة: feminine of الرادف, an active participle from the triliteral ردف; its wazn is فاعل.
(8) واجفة: feminine of واجف, an active participle from the triliteral وجف; its wazn is فاعل.
(10) الحافرة: a name for the road on which a person returns by the way he came, and by it the return in conditions from the end of the matter to its beginning is expressed.. It is on the wazn فاعل in the sense of مفعول, and what is meant by it here is the earth.
(11) نخرة: feminine of نخر, an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the triliteral نخر al-ʿaẓm, bāb fariḥa, when it has decayed; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then kasra.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī): in the saying of the Exalted «يوم ترجف الراجفة».
The attribution to it is figurative, because it is the cause of the quaking.

* Benefits:
- Deletion of the answer to the oath:
It is obligatory to delete it if something that indicates the answer precedes it or surrounds it, as in (زيد قائم والله) ("Zayd is standing, by Allah").
And from it: (إن جاءني زيد والله أكرمته) ("If Zayd comes to me, by Allah, I will honour him"). These are examples in which the answer precedes and so is deleted. Likewise the answer is deleted if something indicating the answer surrounds it, such as: «زيد والله قائم». If you say: (زيد والله إنه قائم), it is possible that the later part is a khabar for the earlier, and it is possible that it is the answer, the clause of the oath and its answer being the khabar. It is permissible in other cases as well, as in the saying of the Exalted in the sūra we are dealing with: (وَالنَّازِعاتِ غَرْقاً. وَالنَّاشِطاتِ نَشْطاً); the answer to the oath is omitted, its implied form being (لتبعثن), as shown by what follows; and this implied element is the operator in the saying of the Exalted (يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الرَّاجِفَةُ), or its operator is the omitted (اذكر) ("remember"). Like it is (ق وَالْقُرْآنِ الْمَجِيدِ), where the answer is implied as (ليهلكن), as shown by (كَمْ أَهْلَكْنا). And like it is (ص وَالْقُرْآنِ ذِي الذِّكْرِ), i.e. (إنه لمعجز).

safi-cedvel:12-12.t:
* I'rab:
(إذا) with tanwīn – a particle of response, with no grammatical position [Note: إذا – with tanwīn – expresses an implied condition, i.e.: "if we are returned to the ḥāfira and that is true, then it is a losing return"].
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is a resumption confirming the preceding clause يقولون.
And the clause: «تلك ... كرّة ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of speech (maqūl al-qawl).

* Morphology:
(خاسرة): feminine of خاسر, an active participle from the triliteral خسر, bāb fariḥa; its wazn is فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī): in the saying of the Exalted «تِلْكَ إِذاً كَرَّةٌ خاسِرَةٌ».
Loss is attributed to the return, while what is meant is its owners. The meaning: if our return to the Resurrection is true, then that return is a losing return.

safi-cedvel:13-14.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive. (إنّما) the restraining and the restrained [kāffa and makfūfa]. (الفاء) the second links to the apodosis of an implied condition. (إذا) of surprise (fujāʾiyya). (بالساهرة) attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم). Clause: «هي زجرة ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: or it is a reason for something implied, said by an implied "say", i.e. the Exalted said: That is not hard, because it is a single cry].
And the clause: «هم بالساهرة ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "when the Trumpet is blown, then behold they ...".

* Morphology:
(13) زجرة: a maṣdar of single occurrence (maṣdar marra) from the triliteral زجر; its wazn is فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn.
(واحدة): feminine of واحد, the name of the first of the arithmetical numbers; its wazn is فاعل.
(14) الساهرة: feminine of الساهر, an adjective of the earth or the open desert because whoever traverses it does not sleep out of fear; its wazn is فاعل.

safi-cedvel:15-26.t:
* I'rab:
(هل) an interrogative particle. (إذ) an adverb of past time in the position of accusative, attached to (حديث). (بالواد) attached to a ḥāl from the third-person pronoun in (ناداه) [Note: or attached to (ناداه)], and the sign of genitive is the kasra implied on the deleted yāʾ, because of the reading in connected speech (waṣl) owing to the meeting of two sākin letters. (طوى) ʿaṭf bayān to الوادي – or a badal from it – genitive..
Clause: «أتاك حديث ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «ناداه ربّه ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «اذهب ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «إنّه طغى ... » has no grammatical position; it is a causal clause.
And the clause: «طغى ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of إنّ.
18- 19 (الفاء) conjunction. (هل) an interrogative particle. (لك) a fronted khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "an inclination" or "a way". (أن) a maṣdar particle governing the accusative.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن تزكّى) is in the position of genitive by (إلى), attached to the implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "an inclination to purify yourself".
(الواو) conjunction. (أهديك) an imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (تزكّى). (إلى ربّك) attached to (أهديك) with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "to knowledge of your Lord". (الفاء) causal. (تخشى) an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of nominative being the ḍamma implied on the alif, and the fāʿil is "you".
And the clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause اذهب.
And the clause: «هل لك (ميل ... ) » is in the position of accusative, the content of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
And the clause: «تزكّى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
And the clause: «أهديك ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تزكّى.
And the clause: «تخشى ... » has no grammatical position; it is a reason for the knowledge.
20- 26 (الفاء) is a conjunction in the five places. (الآية) a second object, accusative. (الواو, ثمّ) two conjunctions. (نكال) a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar of an omitted verb [Note: it is a noun of the maṣdar, i.e. "He made an example of him (nakkala bihi) nakāl".. It may also stand in for the maṣdar because its verb meets it in meaning, so "Allah seized him" is a nakāl.. It is also permissible that it be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi]. (الآخرة) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive – and it is an adjective of an omitted described noun, i.e. "the last word" – and likewise الأولى. (في ذلك) attached to the khabar of إنّ. (اللام) for emphasis. (لمن) attached to an adjective of (عبرة)..
And the clause: «أراه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "so he went to Pharaoh and showed him".
And the clause: «كذّب ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أراه.
And the clause: «عصى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كذّب.
And the clause: «أدبر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كذّب.
And the clause: «يسعى ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the fāʿil of أدبر.
And the clause: «حشر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أدبر.
And the clause: «نادى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause حشر.
And the clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause نادى.
And the clause: «أنا ربّكم ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
And the clause: «أخذه الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قال.
And the clause: «إنّ في ذلك لعبرة ... » has no grammatical position; it is a reason for the seizing [Note: Some exegetes made this clause the answer to the oath with which the sūra began..].
And the clause: «يخشى» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (من).

* Morphology:
(16) الواد: it is written in the muṣḥaf without yāʾ, in observance of its deletion in recitation because of the meeting of two sākin letters.
(18) تزكّى: an imperfect from which one of the two tāʾs has been deleted.. What is mentioned in Sūrat Ṭāhā is a past verb, in which the yāʾ is changed into alif because it is vowelled and what precedes it has fatḥa.
(20) أراه: the first hamza is one of the augment letters in the verb, so it is the hamza of أفعل, and the alif before the hāʾ is the lām of the verb; as for its ʿayn – the hamza, the bare form being رأى – it has been deleted for lightening after transferring its vowel to the rāʾ; the original is أرآه (أرأاه) – with a hamza and then an alif after it – its wazn is أفله [Note: see also verse (55) of Sūrat al-Baqara].
(24) الأعلى: on the pattern of the elative noun, but the elative is not intended by it, rather the description; its wazn is أفعل, and the lām of the word is changed from a yāʾ – being fourth – and its original is a wāw from العلوّ.. the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into alif.

safi-cedvel:27-29.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for interrogation of rebuke. (خلقا) a tamyīz, accusative. (السماء) conjoined to the pronoun mubtadaʾ (أنتم) by the conjunction, and the fāʿil of (بناها) is a pronoun referring to Allah, understood from the context ...
Clause: «أنتم أشدّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «بناها ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «رفع ... » has no grammatical position; it is another explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «سوّاها ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause رفع.
And the clause: «أغطش ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause رفع.
And the clause: «أخرج ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause رفع.

* Morphology:
(أشدّ): an elative from the triliteral شدّ; its wazn is أفعل, and its ʿayn and lām are of one letter.
(خلقا): a maṣdar of the triliteral خلق; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(سمكها): a maṣdar of سمك, i.e. "became thick and dense".. its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(سوّاها): it contains an iʿlāl by substitution, whose analogy is like (بناها): the yāʾ – the lām of the word – was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into alif.
(ضحاها): a name for the time between the sun's rising and noon; its wazn is فعل with ḍamma then fatḥa..
And see verse (98) of al-Aʿrāf.

safi-cedvel:30-33.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (الأرض) a direct object of an omitted verb by way of occupation (ishtighāl), which is explained by what follows, i.e. دحى.. (بعد) an adverb, accusative, attached to the implied (دحى). (منها) attached to (أخرج). (الجبال) like الأرض, i.e. "He fixed the mountains". (متاعا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, i.e. "He gave you enjoyment by that, an enjoyment" [Note: It is permissible that it be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi whose operator is omitted, i.e. "He did that as an enjoyment ..."], so it stands in for the maṣdar because it meets it in derivation. (لكم) attached to (متاعا), and likewise لأنعامكم, which is conjoined to it.
Clause: « (دحى) الأرض ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «دحاها» has no grammatical position; it is explicative (tafsīriyya).
And the clause: «أخرج ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: « (أرسى) الجبال ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause (دحى) الأرض [Note: It may be parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya) if the operator of (متاعا) is the verb أخرج].
And the clause: «أرساها ... » has no grammatical position; it is explicative.

* Morphology:
(30) دحاها: it contains an iʿlāl by substitution like سوّاها [Note: in verse (27) of the sūra]; the alif originates from a wāw or a yāʾ.
(31) مرعاها: originally a noun of place, then used as a majāz mursal for trees, herbage and what a person eats.. it contains an iʿlāl by substitution: the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into alif.. its wazn is مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn.
(32) أرساها: it contains an iʿlāl by substitution; the alif originates from a yāʾ in the augmented form, and from a wāw in the bare form; the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into alif.

* Rhetoric:
Majāz mursal: in the saying of the Exalted «أَخْرَجَ مِنْها ماءَها وَمَرْعاها».
Here المرعى is used for anything eaten, by man and others. It may also be an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), because the discourse is with the deniers of the Gathering, as attested by «أَأَنْتُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقاً». It is as though it were said: O you obstinate ones who are paired with the beasts in enjoying this world and being oblivious of the Hereafter.

safi-cedvel:34-36.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive. (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "he is reckoned" [Note: It is permissible that it be a badal from (إذا), and so be attached to the apodosis]. (ما) a maṣdar particle. (لمن) attached to (برّزت).
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما سعى) is in the position of accusative, a direct object.
Clause: «جاءت الطامّة ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.. and the apodosis is implied, i.e. "people are resurrected".
And the clause: «يتذكّر الإنسان ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi..
And the clause: «سعى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما).
And the clause: «برّزت الجحيم ... » is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause يتذكّر.
And the clause: «يرى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (من).

* Morphology:
(34) الطامّة: a name for the calamity; it came on the pattern of the active participle of the triliteral طمّ, i.e. "rose high and overcame"; the tāʾ is redundant for intensification like the tāʾ of الداهية; its wazn is فاعلة, and its ʿayn and lām are of one letter.

safi-cedvel:37-41.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) a conjunction of ramification (tafrīʿ). (أمّا) a non-jussive-governing conditional particle. (من) a relative in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "is punished". (الفاء) the second is causal. (هي) a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl)..
Clause: «من طغى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause [Note: in verse (34) of the sūra, which is composed of the condition, its verb and its apodosis].
And the clause: «طغى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (من).
And the clause: «آثر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause طغى.
And the clause: «إنّ الجحيم ... المأوى» has no grammatical position; it is a reason for the omitted khabar..
And the apodosis is implied, indicated by the khabar.
40- 41 (الواو) is a conjunction in both places. (أمّا من خاف ... ) like أمّا من طغى [Note: in verse (37) of this sūra]. (عن الهوى) attached to (نهى). (الفاء) causal. (إنّ الجنّة هي المأوى) like إنّ الجحيم هي المأوى [Note: in the preceding verse (39)].
And the clause: «من خاف ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause من طغى.
And the clause: «نهى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause خاف, the ṣila of من.
And the clause: «إنّ الجنّة ... المأوى» has no grammatical position; it is a reason for the omitted khabar..
And the apodosis is implied, indicated by the khabar, namely: "he enters Paradise".

* Morphology:
(37) طغى: it contains an iʿlāl by substitution; its original is طغي, its maṣdar طغيان; the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into alif.
(آثر): the madda is composed of two hamzas, the first with fatḥa and the second sākin (أأثر); its wazn is أفعل, its imperfect يؤثر like أكرم يكرم.
(39) المأوى: a noun of place from the triliteral أوى; its wazn is مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn; it is a lafīf maqrūn (a verb with two weak letters adjacent).

* Rhetoric:
The art of muqābala (antithetical correspondence): in these noble verses, where several antitheses (ṭibāq) occur; and the multiplicity of ṭibāq, as is well known in the science of rhetoric, is called muqābala.

safi-cedvel:42-46.t:
* I'rab:
(عن الساعة) attached to (يسألونك). (أيّان) an interrogative noun in the position of accusative, an adverb of time, attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (مرساها). (فيم) a preposition and an interrogative noun in the position of genitive, attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ أنت. (من ذكراها) attached to the implied khabar. (إلى ربّك) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (منتهاها) ..
Clause: «يسألونك ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «أيّان مرساها ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «فيم أنت ... » has no grammatical position; it is another explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «إلى ربّك منتهاها ... » has no grammatical position; it is a reason for the interrogative that includes the meaning of denial.
45- 46 (إنّما) the restraining and the restrained [kāffa and makfūfa]. (من) a relative in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi. (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil of the negated (يلبثوا). (إلّا) for restriction. (عشيّة) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يلبثوا). (أو) a conjunction.. (ضحاها) conjoined to عشيّة [Note: The annexation of الضحا to the pronoun of العشيّة is because they belong to one day; the connection between them permits the annexation of one to the other].
And the clause: «أنت منذر ... » has no grammatical position; it is another reason.
And the clause: «يخشاها ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (من).
And the clause: «كأنّهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «يرونها ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «لم يلبثوا ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of كأنّ.

* Morphology:
(عشيّة): a noun meaning the evening; its wazn is فعيلة, and the yāʾ of فعيلة and the lām of the word are of one letter.

* Rhetoric:
Explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya): in the saying of the Exalted «أَيَّانَ مُرْساها».
There is an explicit metaphor in the discourse, where "mooring" (irsāʾ) is borrowed, though it is used only for what has weight.

semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {غَرْقاً}: It may be a maṣdar (verbal noun) on the basis of deleting the augments, in the sense of «إغْراقاً» (going to the utmost), made accusative by what precedes it because it coincides with it in meaning; or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. possessing ighrāq. One says: aghraqa fī al-shayʾ, yughriqu fīhi, when he goes deep into it and reaches its utmost limit. From this: the archer aghraqa in the bow, i.e. reached the utmost extent of drawing it.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
«ونَشْطاً» and «وسَبْحاً» and «وسَبْقاً» are all maṣdars (verbal nouns). Al-nashṭ is tying, and al-inshāṭ is untying. One says: nashaṭa the camel, i.e. tied it; and anshaṭahu, i.e. untied it. From this: "as though he were released (unshiṭa) from a hobble". So the hamza [of form IV] is privative. And nashiṭa: he went quickly; from this the wild cows were called nawāshiṭ. Himyān ibn Quḥāfa said:
4480 - أرى همومي تَنْشِطُ المَناشِطا ... الشَّامَ بي طَوْراً وطَوْراً واسِطا
(I see my cares hurry me along the roads: at times to Syria, at times to Wāsiṭ.)
And nashaṭtu the rope, anshiṭuhu, unshūṭa: I tied it [in a slip-knot]; and anshaṭtuhu: I stretched it; and nashaṭa is like anshaṭa. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "They nashiṭ the souls, i.e. take them out, from nashaṭa the bucket from the well when he took it out."
«أَمْراً» is an object of «المُدَبِّرات». It was also said: a ḥāl (circumstantial): they manage it while being commanded; but this is far-fetched. What is meant by these is either groups of angels, or troops of the horses of raiders, or the stars, or the fates of death, or the wild cows and what is like them in their speed, or the souls of the believers.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ}: accusative by an implied verb, which is the response to the oath, its implied form being "you will surely be resurrected (لَتُبْعَثُنَّ)", because what follows indicates it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how have you made «يومَ تَرْجُفُ» an adverb for the implied verb, i.e. 'you will surely be resurrected', when they are not resurrected at the first blowing? I say: the meaning is: you will surely be resurrected in the wide time in which the two blowings occur, and they are resurrected in part of that wide time, namely the time of the other blowing. What indicates this is that His saying «تَتْبَعُها الرَّادِفَةُ» has been made a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الراجفة»." It was also said: the governing word is implied and is not a response [to the oath], i.e. "remember the day when it quakes". On this view there are several views about the response [to the oath]. The first: that it is His saying {إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً} [al-Nāziʿāt: 26]; Abū Bakr ibn al-Anbārī found this ugly because of the long separation. The second: that it is His saying {هَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ موسى} [al-Nāziʿāt: 15], because «هل» means «قد». This is a mistake, because, as I set out for you in {هَلْ أتى} [al-Insān: 1], it does not have the meaning of «قد» except in interrogation, according to what al-Zamakhsharī said. The third: that the response is {تَتْبَعُهَا} [al-Nāziʿāt: 7], and the lām was merely deleted. The origin is "la-yawma tarjufu al-rājifatu tatbaʿuhā"; then the lām was deleted, and the nūn of emphasis did not enter «تَتْبَعُها» because of the separation by the adverb between the implied lām and the verb sworn upon. Similar to it is {لإِلَى الله تُحْشَرُونَ} [Āl ʿImrān: 158]. It was also said: there is a fronting and postponement in the speech, i.e. "On the day the quaking one quakes, followed by the subsequent one—and by those who extract".
Abū Ḥātim said: "It is on the basis of fronting and postponement, as though He said: then at once they will be on the earth's surface—and by those who extract." Ibn al-Anbārī said: "This is wrong, because speech is not opened with the fāʾ." It was also said: «يومَ» is accusative by what «واجِفَةٌ» indicates, i.e. on the day it quakes, [hearts] tremble. It was also said: by what «خاشعة» indicates, i.e. on the day it quakes, [eyes] are humbled.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {تَتْبَعُهَا الرادفة}: It may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الراجفة», or it may be resumptive.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {قُلُوبٌ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject). «يومئذٍ» is accusative by «واجفةٌ», and «واجفة» is an adjective of the hearts, and it is what justifies beginning with an indefinite noun. «أَبْصارُها» is a second mubtadaʾ and «خاشِعة» its khabar (predicate), and it together with its khabar is the khabar of the first «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «وهو وخبرُ الأولِ», evidently for «وهو وخبرُه خبرُ الأولِ»; translated according to the evident sense]». There is a deleted muḍāf in the speech, its implied form being: the eyes of the owners of the hearts. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "That is permissible, i.e. beginning with «قلوب», because it has been specified by His saying «يومئذٍ»." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] replied to him that an adverb of time does not specify concrete bodies, meaning that concrete bodies are not described by it. Al-wājifa is the fearful. One says wajafa yajifu wajīfan; its origin is the agitation and disquiet of the heart. Qays ibn al-Khaṭīm said:
4481 - إنَّ بني جَحْجَبَى وأُسْرَتَهُمْ ... أكبادُنا مِنْ ورائِهم تَجِفُ
(For the Banū Jaḥjabā and their kin our livers tremble behind them.)
/ From Ibn ʿAbbās: «واجِفَةٌ» means fearful, in the dialect of Hamdān. One also says wajaba wajīban, with the one-dotted bāʾ instead of the fāʾ.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {فِي الحافرة}: al-ḥāfira is the path along which a person returns from where he came. One says: he returned fī ḥāfiratihi and ʿalā ḥāfiratihi. Then it is used to express returning in circumstances from the end of a matter to its beginning. [The poet] said:
4482 - أحافِرَةً على صَلَعٍ وشَيْبٍ ... معاذَ اللَّهِ مِنْ سَفَهٍ وعارِ
(Going back to the beginning [of youthful folly], despite baldness and grey hair? Allah forbid such foolishness and disgrace!)
Its origin is that when a person returns along his path, his feet leave a digging (ḥafr) in it. Al-Rāghib said: "His saying «في الحافرة» is a proverbial expression for someone who is sent back to where he came from, i.e. shall we live after we die? It was also said: al-ḥāfira is the earth in which their graves [were made], and its meaning is: shall we indeed be returned while we are in al-ḥāfira, i.e. in the graves? On this view His saying «في الحافرة» is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). One says: so-and-so returned ʿalā ḥāfiratihi, and the old man returned to his ḥāfira, i.e. became decrepit, like His saying {وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إلى أَرْذَلِ العمر} [al-Naḥl: 70]. And their saying 'cash at the ḥāfira' is for what is sold for cash. Its origin is the horse when it is sold: it is said, its hoof (ḥāfir) shall not move until its price is paid. Al-ḥafr is the decay of the teeth: his mouth has ḥafara; and the colt has aḥfara for the second and fourth teeth, i.e. is close to having its incisors or quadrants." End of quotation. Al-ḥāfira: it was said that it is fāʿila in the sense of mafʿūla. It was also said: it is by way of relation (nasab), i.e. possessing digging, and what is meant is the earth. The meaning is: we shall indeed be returned alive in our graves. It was also said: al-ḥāfira is the plural of ḥāfir in the sense of foot, i.e. we shall walk alive on our feet and tread the earth with them. It was also said: it is the beginning of the matter. The merchants say: "Cash fī al-ḥāfira", i.e. at the first bargaining. The poet said:
4483 - آلَيْتُ لا أَنْساكُمُ فاعْلَموا ... حتى تُرَدَّ الناسُ في الحافِرَهْ
(I have sworn not to forget you—know it—until people are returned to their first state.)
Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «في الحَفِرَة» without an alif. It was said: the two have the same meaning. It was also said: it is the earth that has changed and become putrid with its dead and their bodies, from their saying: his teeth ḥafirat, i.e. decayed and changed. The readers' disagreement over these two interrogatives has preceded in Sūrat al-Raʿd. His saying «في الحافِرَة» may be attached to «مَرْدُوْدون», or to something omitted as a ḥāl, as has preceded.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {نَّخِرَةً}: The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Abū Bakr [Shuʿba] read «ناخِرَة» with an alif, and the rest «نَخِرَة» without it. They are like ḥādhir and ḥadhir: fāʿil is for one from whom the action issues, and faʿil for one in whom it is an innate trait or like an innate trait. It was also said: nākhira and nakhira both mean decayed. It was also said: nākhira, i.e. the wind has come to whistle through it, i.e. make a sound; and nakhira, i.e. [the wind] whistles through it constantly. It was also said: nākhira is decayed, and nakhira is crumbling. From Abū ʿAmr: al-nākhira is the one that has not yet crumbled, and al-nakhira is the decayed one. It was also said: al-nākhira is that in which the wind makes a sound, and al-nakhira is the decayed one that has rotted. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "One says: the bone nakhira, so it is nakhir and nākhir, as you say ṭamiʿa, so he is ṭamiʿ and ṭāmiʿ; faʿil is more intensive than fāʿil, and it has been read with it. It is the decayed, hollow [bone] through which the wind passes so that a whistling (nakhīr) is heard from it." I say: from this is the poet's saying:
4484 - وأَخْلَيْتُها مِنْ مُخِّها فكأنَّها ... قواريرُ في أجوافِها الريحُ تَنْخِرُ
(I emptied them of their marrow, so they are like flasks in whose hollows the wind whistles.)
And the rajaz poet said to his horse:
4485 - أَقْدِمْ نَجاحُ إنها الأَساوِرَهْ ... ولا يَهْوْلَنَّكَ رَحْلٌ نادِرَهْ
فإنما قَصْرُك تُرْبُ السَّاهِرَهْ ... ثم تعودُ بعدها في الحافِرَهْ
مِنْ بعدِ ما كنتَ عِظاماً ناخِرَهْ
(Advance, Najāḥ! These are the horsemen; let no fallen saddle frighten you. Your end is but the dust of the earth's surface; then you will return after it to your first state, after you had been hollow, whistling bones.)
Nukhrat al-rīḥ, with ḍamma on the nūn, is the violence of its blowing; and al-nukhra is also the front of the nose of the horse, the donkey and the pig. One says: he smashed his nukhra, i.e. the front of his nose. «إذا» is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. when we are such, shall we be returned and resurrected?

semin-durr:12-12.t: His saying: {تِلْكَ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) by which reference is made to the quaking and the return to al-ḥāfira. «كَرَّةٌ» is its khabar (predicate), and «خاسِرَةٌ» is an adjective, i.e. possessing loss; or loss is attributed to it while what is meant is its people, figuratively. The meaning is: if our return to the Resurrection is true, then that return is a losing return. This is what «إذَنْ» conveys, for it is a particle of response and recompense according to the majority. It was also said: it is sometimes not a response. From al-Ḥasan: «خاسرة» means false.

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {فَإِنَّمَا هِيَ}: «هي» is the pronoun of the return (al-karra), i.e. do not reckon that return difficult for Allah the Exalted. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: to what is His saying «فإنما هي» connected? I say: to something omitted whose meaning is: do not consider it difficult, for it is only a single cry." I say: he means connection in terms of meaning, namely conjunction.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {فَإِذَا هُم}: The surprise and the causation here are both clear. As for al-sāhira, it was said: the surface of the earth, and the desert, described by what happens in it, namely sleeplessness (sahar) due to fear. It was also said: because the mirage flows in it, from their saying "a wakeful (sāhira) spring". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Al-sāhira is the white, level earth; it was named so because the mirage flows in it, from their saying / 'a sāhira spring', i.e. with flowing water, and for its opposite 'sleeping'. Al-Ashʿath ibn Qays said:
4486 - وساهِرَةٍ يُضْحِي السَّرابُ مُجَلِّلاً ... لأَقْطارِها قد جُبْتُها مُتَلَثِّما
(Many a bare plain whose regions the mirage covers by forenoon have I crossed, veiled.)
Or because its inhabitant does not sleep, fearing destruction." End of quotation. Umayya said:
4487 - وفيها لَحْمُ ساهِرَةٍ وبَحْرٍ ... وما فاهوا لهمْ فيها مُقيمُ
(And in it is the flesh of land and sea [creatures], and what they utter is ever-abiding for them there.)
He means: the flesh of the animals of a sāhira land. Abū Kabīr al-Hudhalī said:
4488 - يَرْتَدْنَ ساهِرَةً كأنَّ جَميمَها ... وعَمِيْمَها أسْدافُ ليلٍ مُظْلِمٍ
(They roam a bare plain whose sprouting and dense herbage seem like the folds of a dark night.)
Al-Rāghib said: "It is the surface of the earth. It was also said: the land of the Resurrection. Its true meaning is that on which treading is abundant, as though it had stayed awake (sahirat) from that—alluding to something like the poet's saying:
4489 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... تَحَرَّكَ يَقْظانُ الترابِ ونائِمُهْ
(… the waking and the sleeping dust stirred.)
And al-asharān («الأَسْهَران») are two veins in the nose." End of quotation. Al-sāhūr is the sheath of the moon into which it enters at its eclipse. [The poet] said:
4490 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... أو شُقَّةٌ أُخْرِجَتْ مِنْ بَطْنِ ساهُوْرِ
(… or a slice [of moon] brought out from the belly of its sheath.)
i.e. this woman is like a piece of the moon. Umayya said:
4491 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... قَمَرٌ وساهُوْرٌ يُسَلُّ ويُغْمَدُ
(… a moon and a sheath, drawn out and sheathed.)

semin-durr:16-16.t: His saying: {إِذْ نَادَاهُ}: «إذ» is accusative by «حديثُ», not by «أتاك», because their times differ. The discussion of {طُوًى} [verse 12] has preceded in Ṭā Hā.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {اذهب}: It may be an explanation of the calling. It may be on the basis of an implied verb of saying. It was also said: it is on the basis of a deleted «أَنْ», i.e. "that: go". The reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] «أَنْ اذْهَبْ» supports this. This «أَنْ», whether overt or implied, may be explicative (tafsīriyya), or it may be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), i.e. He called him with such-and-such.

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {هَل لَّكَ}: [It is] the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), and «إلى أَنْ» is attached to that mubtadaʾ; this is a common deletion. The implied form is: "Have you a way to purification?" Similar is "Have you [an inclination] for good?", meaning: have you a desire for good. The poet said:
4492 - فهل لكمُ فيها إليَّ فإنَّني ... بَصيرٌ بما أَعْيا النِّطاسِيَّ حِذْيَما
(Have you [any wish] to bring it to me? For I am skilled in what baffled the expert physician Ḥidhyam.)
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Since the meaning is 'I invite you', He brought «إلى»." This contributes nothing to the iʿrāb. Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr read with doubling of the zāy in «تَزَّكَّى», and of the ṣād in «تَصَّدَّى» in the following sūra. The origin is tatazakkā and tataṣaddā; the two Ḥaramīs [Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr] assimilated, and the rest deleted [one tāʾ], as in {تَنَزَّلُ} [al-Qadr: 4]. The disagreement over which of the two is the deleted one has preceded.

semin-durr:23-23.t: His saying: {فَحَشَرَ فنادى}: The objects of both are not mentioned, since what is meant is that he did that; or the implied form is: he gathered his people and called them. His saying «فقال» is an explanation of the calling.

semin-durr:25-25.t: His saying: {نَكَالَ الآخرة}: It may be a maṣdar (absolute object) of «أَخَذَ», with the figurative usage either in the verb—i.e. He made an example by the seizing, the exemplary punishment of the Hereafter—or in the maṣdar, i.e. He seized him with a seizing of exemplary punishment. It may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. for the sake of making an example of him. Making it a ḥāl (circumstantial) is weak because it is definite, and interpreting it like the interpretation of «جَهْدَك» and «طاقَتَك» is not according to analogy. It may be a maṣdar emphasising the content of the preceding clause, i.e. Allah made an example of him with the exemplary punishment of the Hereafter; al-Zamakhsharī said this, and he made it like {وَعْدَ الله} [al-Nisāʾ: 122] and {صِبْغَةَ الله} [al-Baqara: 138]. Al-nakāl is equivalent to al-tankīl, as al-salām is in the sense of al-taslīm. The latter and the former are either the two abodes, or the two utterances: the latter is his saying {أَنَاْ رَبُّكُمُ الأعلى} [al-Nāziʿāt: 24], and the former {مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُمْ مِّنْ إله غَيْرِي} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 38]; the qualified noun was deleted because it is known.

semin-durr:27-27.t: His saying: {أَمِ السمآء}: conjoined to «أنتم». His saying «بناها» is an explication of the manner of His creating it. So the pause is at «السماء», and one begins with what follows it. Its parallel is what has passed in al-Zukhruf [verse 58]: {أَآلِهَتُنَا خَيْرٌ أَمْ هُوَ}.

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا}: an explicative clause of the manner of the building. Al-samk is height. Its meaning in the verse, as al-Zamakhsharī said: "He made the extent of its going in the direction of height long and lofty." Samaktu the thing: I raised it in the air. And it samaka, i.e. rose, sumūkan; so it is intransitive and transitive. A sāmik tāmik hump, i.e. high and raised. The simāk of a house is that with which you raised it. Al-simāk is a well-known star, and they are two: the armed one (rāmiḥ) and the unarmed one (aʿzal). The poet said:
4493 - إنَّ الذي سَمَكَ السماءَ بنى لنا ... بيتاً دعائِمُه أعَزُّ وأَطْوَلُ
(He who raised the sky has built for us a house whose pillars are mightier and taller.)

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {وَأَغْطَشَ}: i.e. He darkened, in the dialect of Anmār and Ashʿar. One says: the night ghaṭisha, and I ghaṭṭashtuhu and aghṭashtuhu. [The poet] said:
4494 - عَقَرْتُ لهُمْ ناقتي مَوْهِناً ... فلَيْلُهُمُ مُدْلَهِمٌّ غَطِشْ
(I slaughtered my she-camel for them late at night, while their night was pitch-black and dark.)
And a night that is aghṭash, and a ghaṭshāʾ night. Al-Rāghib said: "Its origin is from al-aghṭash, the one whose eye is bleary. From it is a ghaṭshā desert, in which one finds no way. And al-taghāṭush is feigning blindness." End of quotation. One also says aghṭasha al-layl, intransitive, like aẓlama; so afʿala in it is transitive / and intransitive.
His saying: {وَأَخْرَجَ ضُحَاهَا}: there is a deletion in it, i.e. the forenoon of its sun; or He attributed the night and the forenoon to it because of the connection between it and them.

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ}: «بعد» is in its basic sense of posteriority. There is no contradiction between it and the verse of Fuṣṣilat, because He created the earth not spread out, then created the sky, then spread out the earth. The saying of Abū ʿUbayda that "it means 'before'" is rejected by the scholars. One says daḥā yadḥū daḥwan and daḥā yadḥī daḥyan, i.e. spread out; so it is among the [roots] with wāw and with yāʾ, and is written with alif and with yāʾ. From it the nest of the ostrich was called udḥuww and udḥiyy, because it is spread out on the ground. Umayya said:
4495 - وبَثَّ الخَلْقَ فيها إذ دَحاها ... فهم قُطَّانُها حتى التَّنادِي
(He spread the creatures in it when He spread it out, and they are its dwellers until the Day of Calling.)
It was also said: daḥā means levelled. Zayd ibn Nufayl said:
4496 - وأَسْلَمْتُ وَجْهِيْ لِمَنْ أَسْلَمَتْ ... له الأرضُ تَحْمِلُ صَخْراً ثقالاً
دَحاها فلَمَّا اسْتَوَتْ شَدَّها ... بأَيْدٍ وأَرْسى عليها الجِبالا
(I have submitted my face to Him to whom the earth submitted, bearing heavy rocks; He spread it out, and when it was level He made it firm with might and set the mountains firmly upon it.)
The majority read «الأرض» and «الجبال» in the accusative by an implied verb explained by what follows, and this is preferred because a verbal clause precedes. Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Abī ʿAbla, Abū Ḥaywa, Abū al-Sammāl and ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read both in the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and ʿĪsā read «الأرض» alone in the nominative.

semin-durr:31-31.t: His saying: {أَخْرَجَ}: There are two aspects to it. The first: that it is an explanation. The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why did He not put a conjunction before «أَخْرَجَ»? I say: there are two aspects to it. The first: that «دحاها» means He spread it out and prepared it for habitation; then He explained the preparation by what is indispensable for its habitation to be possible: arranging the matter of food and drink and the possibility of settling on it. The second: that «أَخْرَجَ» is a ḥāl with «قد» implied, like His saying {أَوْ جَآءُوكُمْ حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 90]." I say: implying «قد» is the view of the majority, and the Kufans and al-Akhfash disagreed.

semin-durr:33-33.t: His saying: {مَتَاعاً}: the majority read it in the accusative, as an object of purpose (mafʿūl lahu), or as a maṣdar of an implied governing verb, that is: "He gave you enjoyment". Al-marʿā is originally a place, a time or a maṣdar; here it is a maṣdar in the sense of the object (what is pastured), and with respect to human beings it is a metaphor.

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying: {فَإِذَا جَآءَتِ}: there are several views on its answer. First, his saying «فأمَّا مَنْ طغى», like "when the Banū Tamīm come to you, then as for the disobedient, humiliate him, and as for the obedient, honour him." It is also said that it is omitted. Al-Zamakhsharī implied: "then the matter is so", that is, "then Hell is his abode". Someone else implied: [«انقسم الراؤون قسمين» — Translator's note: the source text reads "the onlookers divided into two groups"]. It is also said: "they saw" or "they knew". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The word governing it is its answer, and that is the meaning of his saying «يومَ يتَذَكَّرَ الإِنسانُ»." Al-ṭāmma is the calamity that overwhelms (taṭummu) other calamities by its greatness. Al-ṭamm is burial; from it, ṭamma al-sayl al-rakiyya (the flood buried the well). In the proverb: "the valley flowed and overwhelmed the villages". What is meant by it in the Qur'an is the second blowing [Translator's note: the source prints «النخفة», evidently a misprint for «النفخة»], because that is what brings it about.

semin-durr:35-35.t: His saying: {يَوْمَ يَتَذَكَّرُ}: a badal (substitute) from «إذا», or accusative by an implied verb, that is: "I mean the day when", or: "the day when he remembers" proceeds in such-and-such a way.

semin-durr:36-36.t: His saying: {وَبُرِّزَتِ}: the majority read it passive with shadda, and «لِمَنْ يرى» with the third-person yāʾ. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, ʿĀʾisha and ʿIkrima read it active and light, and «ترى» with the tāʾ from above (second or feminine). They allowed that the tāʾ of «ترى» be feminine, with the pronoun in «ترى» referring to the Hell, like His saying: {إِذَا رَأَتْهُمْ مِّن مَّكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ} [al-Furqān: 12], or that it be for address, that is: "you see, Muḥammad". ʿAbd Allāh read «لِمَنْ رأى» as a past verb.

semin-durr:39-39.t:
His saying: {هِيَ المأوى}: either "it is the abode for him" or "it is his abode", with «أل» standing in the place of the pronoun, which is the opinion of the Kufans. The verification of this disagreement and the refutation of its proponent was given to you earlier by his saying:
4497 - رَحِيْبٌ قِطابُ الجَيْبِ منها رَفيقةٌ ... بجَسَّ النَّدامى بَضَّةُ المُتَجَرِّدِ
(Wide is the opening of her collar, gentle in the touch of her drinking companions, delicate of body when unclothed.)
since if «أل» were a substitute for the pronoun, the two would not have been joined in this verse. One of these two interpretations is needed in the noble verse for the sake of the referent linking the clause that is the khabar (predicate) back to the mubtadaʾ (subject). What made the omission of the referent acceptable is that the word falls at the head of a verse-ending (fāṣila). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning is: Hell is his abode, as you say to a man: / «ghuḍḍa al-ṭarf» (lower the gaze). The alif and lām are not a substitute for the annexation, but since it is known that the transgressor is the owner of the abode, and that a man does not lower another's gaze, the annexation was left out; and the alif and lām enter «المَأْوَى» and «الطَّرْفِ» for definiteness because both are known."
The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "This is speech from which the linking referent to the mubtadaʾ is not obtained, since he denied the Kufan position and did not imply a pronoun as the Basrans did; so he sought to obtain the link without a link." I say: his saying "but since it is known" to its end is exactly the Basran view, and I do not know how that escaped him.

semin-durr:43-43.t: His saying: {فِيمَ أَنتَ}: «فيم» is a fronted khabar (predicate) and «أنت» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); «مِنْ ذِكْراها» is attached to what the khabar is attached to. The meaning: in what are you with respect to mentioning it, that is: you have no part in mentioning it to them and explaining its time. Al-Zamakhsharī reported from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her: "He, peace be upon him, kept mentioning the Hour and being asked about it until this was revealed." He said: on this it is an expression of wonder at the frequency of his mentioning it, as if it were said: in what preoccupation and concern am I regarding mentioning it and being asked about it. It is also said: the pause is on his saying «فيمَ», which is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: "what is this questioning?", and then it begins with His saying {أَنتَ مِن ذِكْرَاهَا}, that is: your being sent, while you are the seal of the prophets and the last of the messengers, sent at the very breath of the Hour, is a mention among its mentions and a sign among its signs; so that suffices them as evidence of its nearness, its approach, and preparing for it, and there is no sense in their asking about it. Al-Zamakhsharī said this, and it is fine speech, were it not that it contradicts the apparent sense and disrupts the structure of the sentence.

semin-durr:45-45.t: His saying: {مُنذِرُ مَن}: the majority read it with the adjective annexed to its object for lightness. ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, Abū Jaʿfar, Ṭalḥa and Ibn Muḥayṣin read it with tanwīn. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the original, and annexation is for lightness, and both are suitable for the present and the future. If the past is intended, then only annexation is possible, as in your saying: huwa mundhiru Zaydin amsi (he is the warner of Zayd yesterday)." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "His saying «it is the original», meaning tanwīn, is a view that others have said", then the Shaykh preferred that the original is annexation. He said: "because governing is only by resemblance, and annexation is the origin in nouns." Then he said: "His saying 'only annexation' involves a detail and a disagreement mentioned in grammar." I say: he is not obliged to mention the place of agreement; rather, these two that he mentioned are the view of the majority of people. [Translator's note: the source reads «اللذن» here, apparently a misprint for «اللذين».]

semin-durr:46-46.t: His saying: {أَوْ ضُحَاهَا}: that is, the forenoon of that evening. He annexed the adverbial to the pronoun of the other adverbial figuratively and by extension, and mentioned both because they are the two ends of the day. What made this annexation good is that the word falls as a verse-ending (fāṣila).

ukberi-tibyan:1-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالنَّازِعَاتِ غَرْقًا (١) وَالنَّاشِطَاتِ نَشْطًا (٢) وَالسَّابِحَاتِ سَبْحًا (٣) فَالسَّابِقَاتِ سَبْقًا (٤) فَالْمُدَبِّرَاتِ أَمْرًا (٥) يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الرَّاجِفَةُ (٦) تَتْبَعُهَا الرَّادِفَةُ (٧)).
(غَرْقًا) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) according to the meaning, because «النَّازِع» is the one who goes to the utmost in drawing the arrow, or in pulling out the soul; it is a maṣdar with its augment dropped, i.e. «إِغْرَاقًا». (أَمْرًا) is an object. It is also said to be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. they manage [affairs] as ones commanded. (يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ) is an object, i.e. «اذْكُرْ» (remember).
It may also be an adverb (ẓarf) for what «وَاجِفَةٌ» or «خَاشِعَةٌ» indicates, i.e. on the day when [hearts] tremble.
(تَتْبَعُهَا) is resumptive (mustaʾnaf), or a ḥāl from «الرَّاجِفَة».

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَقُولُونَ أَئِنَّا لَمَرْدُودُونَ فِي الْحَافِرَةِ (١٠)).
The words of the Exalted (يَقُولُونَ): i.e. the owners of the hearts and the eyes say.

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (اذْهَبْ إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَى (١٧)).
The words of the Exalted (اذْهَبْ): i.e. He said: "Go".
It is also said that the implied form is «أَنِ اذْهَبْ» (that go), and «أَنْ» was omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَقُلْ هَلْ لَكَ إِلَى أَنْ تَزَكَّى (١٨)).
The words of the Exalted (إِلَى أَنْ تَزَكَّى): since the meaning is «أَدْعُوكَ» (I invite you), He brought «إِلَى».

ukberi-tibyan:25-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأَخَذَهُ اللَّهُ نَكَالَ الْآخِرَةِ وَالْأُولَى (٢٥) إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِمَنْ يَخْشَى (٢٦)).
