The words of the Exalted (نَكَالَ الْآخِرَةِ): there are two views on its accusative. First: it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). Second: it is a maṣdar (absolute object), because «أَخَذَهُ» and «نَكَّلَ بِهِ» (He made an example of him) have the same meaning here.
As for the answer to the oath, it is said that it is «إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً»; and it is also said that it is omitted, its implied form being «لَتُبْعَثُنَّ» (you will surely be resurrected).

ukberi-tibyan:27-33.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَأَنْتُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقًا أَمِ السَّمَاءُ بَنَاهَا (٢٧) رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا فَسَوَّاهَا (٢٨) وَأَغْطَشَ لَيْلَهَا وَأَخْرَجَ ضُحَاهَا (٢٩) وَالْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ دَحَاهَا (٣٠) أَخْرَجَ مِنْهَا مَاءَهَا وَمَرْعَاهَا (٣١) وَالْجِبَالَ أَرْسَاهَا (٣٢) مَتَاعًا لَكُمْ وَلِأَنْعَامِكُمْ (٣٣)).
The words of the Exalted (أَمِ السَّمَاءُ): it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. «أَمِ السَّمَاءُ أَشَدُّ» (or is the heaven stronger), and «بَنَاهَا» is resumptive (mustaʾnaf). It is also said to be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted [khabar].
(وَالْأَرْضَ) is accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. «وَدَحَا الْأَرْضَ» (and He spread the earth); likewise «الْجِبَالَ», i.e. «وَأَرْسَى الْجِبَالَ» (and He fixed the mountains). (مَتَاعًا) is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or a maṣdar.

ukberi-tibyan:34-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِذَا جَاءَتِ الطَّامَّةُ الْكُبْرَى (٣٤) يَوْمَ يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنْسَانُ مَا سَعَى (٣٥)).
The words of the Exalted (فَإِذَا جَاءَتِ): what governs it is its apodosis (jawāb), which is the meaning of the words of the Exalted «يَوْمَ يَتَذَكَّرُ».

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِنَّ الْجَحِيمَ هِيَ الْمَأْوَى (٣٩)).
The words of the Exalted (هِيَ الْمَأْوَى): i.e. it is the refuge for him. This [implied «لَهُ»] is indispensable, so that a pronoun in the khabar (predicate) refers back to «مَنْ». The same applies to the second «الْمَأْوَى».

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَهَا لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إِلَّا عَشِيَّةً أَوْ ضُحَاهَا (٤٦)).
The hāʾ in «ضُحَاهَا» is the pronoun of «الْعَشِيَّة», like your saying «فِي لَيْلَةٍ وَيَوْمِهَا» (in a night and its day).

zajjaj:1-2.t:
Sūrat al-Nāziʿāt
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿والنّازِعاتِ غَرْقًا﴾ ﴿والنّاشِطاتِ نَشْطًا﴾: it was said in the exegesis: by it are meant the angels who pull out the soul of the unbeliever and draw it out forcibly, so that the departure of his soul becomes hard for him.

zajjaj:3-4.t: His saying: ﴿والسّابِحاتِ سَبْحًا﴾ ﴿فالسّابِقاتِ سَبْقًا﴾: the souls of the believers, which go out with ease. It was also said: ﴿والنّازِعاتِ غَرْقًا﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 1] are the bows; ﴿والنّاشِطاتِ نَشْطًا﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 2] are the lassos (al-awhāq); ﴿والسّابِحاتِ سَبْحًا﴾ are the ships; ﴿فالسّابِقاتِ سَبْقًا﴾ are the horses.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
﴿فالمُدَبِّراتِ أمْرًا﴾
«فالمُدَبِّراتِ أمْرًا» are the angels: Jibrīl, Mīkāʾīl, Isrāfīl and the Angel of Death. Jibrīl is in charge of revelation and the sending down (of scripture), Mīkāʾīl of the rain and the vegetation, Isrāfīl of the Trumpet, and the Angel of Death of taking the souls. It was also said: ﴿والنّازِعاتِ غَرْقًا﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 1] are the stars that move from place to place; likewise ﴿والسّابِحاتِ سَبْحًا﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 3] are the stars that swim in the celestial sphere, as He said: ﴿وَكُلٌّ في فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 40]; and likewise ﴿فالسّابِقاتِ سَبْقًا﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 4]. As for ﴿فالمُدَبِّراتِ أمْرًا﴾, they are the angels. It was also said: ﴿فالسّابِقاتِ سَبْقًا﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 4] are the angels who outstrip the devils with the revelation to the prophets. All of this has come in the exegesis, and Allah knows best the reality of that.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الرّاجِفَةُ﴾ ﴿تَتْبَعُها الرّادِفَةُ﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 7]: «تَرْجُفُ» means it moves with a violent movement. It was also said: «اَلرّاجِفَةُ» is the first blast (of the Trumpet), with which all creatures die.

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿تَتْبَعُها الرّادِفَةُ﴾: it was said: the second blast, with which creatures are resurrected. It is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَنُفِخَ في الصُّورِ فَصَعِقَ مَن في السَّماواتِ ومَن في الأرْضِ إلا مَن شاءَ اللَّهُ ثُمَّ نُفِخَ فِيهِ أُخْرى فَإذا هم قِيامٌ يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ [al-Zumar: 68]. «يَوْمَ» is accusative according to the meaning: "hearts on that day will be throbbing, on the day the quaking quakes." The meaning of «واجِفَةٌ» is: violently agitated.

zajjaj:9-9.t: ﴿أبْصارُها خاشِعَةٌ﴾: abased. The answer (jawāb) to «والنّازِعاتِ» — and Allah knows best — is omitted. The meaning is as though He swore and said: "By these things, you will surely be resurrected." The proof of that is His saying: ﴿يَقُولُونَ أإنّا لَمَرْدُودُونَ في الحافِرَةِ﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 10], that is: "Shall we be returned to life after death, when we are decayed bones?", that is: shall we be returned and resurrected? One says «رَجَعَ فُلانٌ في حافِرَتِهِ» when he returns along the road by which he came. It was read «نَخِرَةً» and «ناخِرَةً»; «ناخِرَةً» is more common in reading and better, because the ends of the verses resemble one another: «اَلْحافِرَةِ», «ناخِرَةً», «خاسِرَةٌ». «نَخِرَةً» is good too: one says «نَخِرَ العَظْمُ، يَنْخَرُ، فَهو نَخِرٌ» ("the bone decayed, it decays, so it is decayed"), like «عَفِنَ الشَّيْءُ، يَعْفَنُ، فَهو عَفِنٌ» ("the thing rotted…, so it is rotten"). «ناخِرَةٌ» is in the sense of: hollow bones in which, from the blowing of the wind, something like a snorting (nakhīr) arises. And «ناخِرَةً» is permissible just as you say «بَلِيَ الشَّيْءُ، وبَلِيَتِ العِظامُ، فَهي بالِيَةٌ» ("the thing wore out, and the bones wore out, so they are worn out").

zajjaj:12-12.t: ﴿قالُوا تِلْكَ إذًا كَرَّةٌ خاسِرَةٌ﴾, that is: this return is a return of loss; the meaning is: "its people are losers." Then He, Mighty and Majestic, made known how easy the resurrection is for Him, saying: ﴿فَإنَّما هي زَجْرَةٌ واحِدَةٌ﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 13] ﴿فَإذا هم بِالسّاهِرَةِ﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 14]. «اَلسّاهِرَةُ» is the face of the earth.

zajjaj:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿بِالوادِ المُقَدَّسِ طُوًى﴾, that is: the blessed. It was read «طُوى اذْهَبْ» without nunation, and «طُوًى» with nunation, and it was read «طِوًى» with kasra on the ṭāʾ. «طُوًى» is the name of the valley in which Allah spoke to Moses. Whoever gives it nunation treats it like «نُغَرٌ» and «صُرَدٌ» when you name a masculine thing with it. Whoever does not give it nunation does so on one of two grounds. One of them is that it is the name of the tract (al-buqʿa) which contains the valley, as He said: ﴿فِي البُقْعَةِ المُبارَكَةِ مِنَ الشَّجَرَةِ﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 30]. And it was said that it is prevented from nunation because it is deflected (maʿdūl), like «عُمَرُ»: it is as though «طُوى» was deflected from «طاوٍ», just as «عُمَرُ» was deflected from «عامِرٌ». Whoever said «طِوًى» with kasra takes it in the sense "sanctified time after time", as Ṭarafa ibn al-ʿAbd said:
؎أعاذِلَ إنَّ اللَّوْمَ في غَيْرِ كُنْهِهِ ∗∗∗ عَلَيَّ طِوًى مِن غَيِّكِ المُتَرَدِّدِ
(O reproaching woman, blame misplaced is heaped on me again and again, from your recurring folly.)
That is: the blame repeated against me.

zajjaj:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿فَأراهُ الآيَةَ الكُبْرى﴾: it means the hand which he drew out shining, without any blemish.

zajjaj:25-25.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَأخَذَهُ اللَّهُ نَكالَ الآخِرَةِ والأُولى﴾: «نَكالَ» is accusative as an emphasising maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of «أخَذَهُ اللَّهُ» is: He made an exemplary punishment of him, the exemplary punishment of the last and the first, that is: He drowned him in this world and will punish him in the Hereafter. It has come in the exegesis that ﴿نَكالَ الآخِرَةِ والأُولى﴾ is the punishment for his saying ﴿ما عَلِمْتُ لَكم مِن إلَهٍ غَيْرِي﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 38] and his saying ﴿أنا رَبُّكُمُ الأعْلى﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 24]; so Allah punished him in exemplary fashion for these two statements.

zajjaj:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿أمِ السَّماءُ بَناها﴾: one of the grammarians said: «بَناها» is part of the ṣila (relative clause) of «اَلسَّماءُ»; the meaning is "or the one which He built". Others said: «اَلسَّماءُ» is not among the things that take a ṣila; rather the meaning is: "Are you harder to create, or is the heaven harder to create?!" Then He made clear how He created it, saying: ﴿بَناها﴾ ﴿رَفَعَ سَمْكَها فَسَوّاها﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 28] ﴿وَأغْطَشَ لَيْلَها﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 29], that is: He made its night dark.

zajjaj:29-29.t: ﴿وَأخْرَجَ ضُحاها﴾: He made its light appear by means of the sun.

zajjaj:30-30.t: His saying: ﴿والأرْضَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ دَحاها﴾: the reading is with «والأرْضَ» in the accusative, in the sense "and He spread out the earth after that"; He explained this implied (muḍmar) verb by saying ﴿دَحاها﴾, as you say «ضَرَبْتُ زَيْدًا وعَمْرًا أكْرَمْتُهُ» ("I struck Zayd, and ʿAmr — I honoured him"). It has also been read «والأرْضُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ دَحاها» in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). The accusative is better, because conjoining a verb to a verb is nicer; so it is in the sense: He built it, and did, and did, and spread out the earth after that.

zajjaj:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿والجِبالَ أرْساها﴾: the explanation of the accusative of الجِبال is like the explanation of the accusative of الأرْض. Likewise the nominative is permissible, and it has been read so in «اَلْجِبالَ», on the explanation given for «والأرْضُ». The meaning of ﴿أرْساها﴾ is: He made them firm.

zajjaj:33-33.t: His saying: ﴿مَتاعًا لَكم ولأنْعامِكُمْ﴾: «مَتاعًا لَّكم» is accusative in the sense of His saying: "He brought forth from it its water and its pasture for your enjoyment", because the meaning of «أخْرَجَ مِنها ماءَها ومَرْعاها» is "He gave enjoyment by that".

zajjaj:34-34.t: His saying: ﴿فَإذا جاءَتِ الطّامَّةُ الكُبْرى﴾: when the Shout comes that overwhelms (taṭummu) everything — the Shout with which the resurrection, the reckoning, the requital, the punishment and the mercy take place.

zajjaj:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأمّا مَن طَغى﴾ ﴿وَآثَرَ الحَياةَ الدُّنْيا﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 38] ﴿فَإنَّ الجَحِيمَ هي المَأْوى﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 39]: this is the answer to "when the great overwhelming calamity comes" — "then the matter is thus". The meaning of «هِيَ المَأْوى» is: it is the refuge for him. Some said: the alif and lām are a substitute for the hāʾ (pronoun); the meaning is "then it is his refuge", because the alif and lām are a substitute for the hāʾ. This is as you say to a person: «غُضَّ الطَّرْفَ يا هَذا» ("lower the gaze, you!"), and the alif and lām stand in as a substitute for the kāf, even though the meaning is «غُضَّ طَرْفَكَ» ("lower your gaze"), because the one addressed knows that you are not commanding him to lower someone else's gaze. The poet said:
؎فَغُضَّ الطَّرْفَ إنَّكَ مِن نُمَيْرٍ ∗∗∗ فَلا كَعْبًا بَلَغْتَ ولا كِلابا
(So lower your gaze, for you are of Numayr; you have reached the rank neither of Kaʿb nor of Kilāb.)
Likewise the meaning of ﴿فَإنَّ الجَنَّةَ هي المَأْوى﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 41] is according to that explanation.

zajjaj:42-42.t: His saying: ﴿أيّانَ مُرْساها﴾: its meaning is "when is its occurring and its arriving?" The meaning of ﴿إلى رَبِّكَ مُنْتَهاها﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 44] is: the final knowledge of it.

zajjaj:45-45.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّما أنْتَ مُنْذِرُ مَن يَخْشاها﴾ — it was also read «مُنْذِرٌ» with nunation, in the sense: "you are only in the state of warning whoever fears it, and you will also warn in the future whoever fears it." With «مُفْعِلٌ» and «فاعِلٌ» (participle patterns), when either of them — or what has their meaning — refers to the future or the present, you give it nunation, because it stands in place of the verb, and the verb can only be indefinite. Omitting the nunation is also permissible by way of resumption (istiʾnāf), while the meaning is that of its being present — he means the presence of the nunation. But if it refers to the past, it takes no nunation at all: you say «أنْتَ مُنْذِرٌ زَيْدًا», that is: "you warned Zayd."
«[Translator's note: the source reads «عَلى الِاسْتِئْنافِ» ("by way of resumption") where one expects «الِاسْتِخْفاف» ("lightening"); and its final example «أنْتَ مُنْذِرٌ زَيْدًا», given for the past, is printed with nunation and an accusative object, contrary to the rule just stated (one would expect «أنْتَ مُنْذِرُ زَيْدٍ»). Both are translated as written and flagged here.]»

zajjaj:46-46.t: His saying: ﴿إلا عَشِيَّةً أوْ ضُحاها﴾: this alif and hāʾ (-hā) refer back to ﴿عَشِيَّةً﴾. The meaning of «إلّا عَشِيَّةً أوْ ضُحاها» is "or the forenoon of the evening": you have annexed the forenoon (al-ḍuḥā) to the evening (al-ʿashiyya). The early morning, the evening, the forenoon and the late morning belong to the day in which they occur. So when you say «أتَيْتُكَ صَباحًا ومَساءَهُ» ("I came to you in a morning and its evening") or «مَساءً وصَباحَهُ» ("an evening and its morning"), the meaning is: "I came to you in a morning and an evening following the morning," and "I came to you in an evening and a morning following the evening."
